Latheport.description: Convert, compress, edit or extract any file. Drop it in, pick a format, done. Was ConvertAll.

releases.name: Latheport 1.5.1
releases.body:
**Download:** `Latheport-1.5.1-windows.zip` below. Unzip it and run `Latheport\Latheport.exe`. Nothing to install. Keep `Latheport.exe` next to its `_internal` folder. Already on 1.5.0? Use *Update now* in the window. Coming from ConvertAll? Your settings, presets, watch folders and right-click menu come along the first time Latheport opens.

### 2026-11-12: Latheport 1.5.1, faster 7z, Open with Latheport, fixes for the move from ConvertAll

In numbers (the built 1.5.0 and 1.5.1 taking turns on the same PC): Latheport's own 78 MB download from zip to 7z in 11.2 s and 10.8 s instead of 60.2 s and 59.4 s, 5.4 times faster. Updating from 1.5.0 with *Update now*: the new window was up 10 s after the old one opened.

- **The right-click entry is now Open with Latheport** (it was Convert with Latheport): files and folders open in the window, ready to convert. Archives still get Extract and 3D models View. An existing menu changes the first time 1.5.1 opens.
- **Making a 7z is 5.4 times faster**, packed on three quarters of the cores (8 at most) instead of one: Latheport's own 78 MB download (187 MB unpacked) from zip to 7z took 11.2 s and 10.8 s instead of 60.2 s and 59.4 s (the built apps taking turns; with other programs busy on the same PC, packing alone took 29 s instead of 79 s). The 7z is 1.3% bigger (55.8 MB instead of 55.0 MB), opens in 7-Zip, Windows' own tar and py7zr with every file the same, and still has the x86 filter and LZMA2 it had. The status line now counts the megabytes packed (*packing 120 of 187 MB*): before, it stopped at the end of unpacking and then sat there for a minute. Cancel now stops packing within a moment too; before, it waited until the 7z was finished.
- **Fixed: the Start menu shortcut kept starting a copy that had been moved or deleted.** It now follows Latheport the next time you open it from its new folder, as the right-click menu already did.
- **Fixed: settings left behind when moving from ConvertAll.** They were only carried into a Latheport with no settings at all, so one value set first (by a run from source, say) kept watch folders and the rest behind for good. Now every setting Latheport doesn't have yet comes along, once; Latheport's own stay.
- **Fixed: a white bar along the top of the window** after dragging it down from maximised (also after double-clicking its header or pressing Win+Down to restore it). The window kept the margin Windows puts round a maximised window: 8 px on every side, white along the top. It's now gone as soon as Windows restores the window (measured with a real drag: 8 px to 0, white top row 100% to 0%). The ☐ button was never affected.
- **Docs: "Do you want to open this file?" on a downloaded archive.** The README now explains it: Windows asks this when another program (DAEMON Tools, for one) owns that kind of archive without marking it safe. Click *Open* and the extraction goes ahead.

releases.name: Latheport 1.5.0
releases.body:
**Download:** `Latheport-1.5.0-windows.zip` below. Unzip it and run `Latheport\Latheport.exe`. Nothing to install. Keep `Latheport.exe` next to its `_internal` folder. Coming from ConvertAll? Your settings, presets, watch folders and right-click menu come along the first time Latheport opens. ### 2026-11-12: Latheport 1.5.0 (was ConvertAll), a photo editor, a video timeline, PDF tools, smart tools, no Ghostscript needed In numbers, against ConvertAll 1.4.0 (both built, the same files on the same PC, taking turns, best of 3): 25 PostScript files to PDF in 2.77 s instead of 4.94 s (1.8x), with no Ghostscript to install (24 MB less); 20 DjVu books to PDF in 61.7 s instead of 76.3 s; 12 RAW photos to PNG in 60.0 s instead of 65.5 s. The download is 78.3 MB, against 77.0 MB for 1.4.0, with the editor, the timeline and the smart tools in it (the smart tools' models download on first use). - **Fixed: text that sat a little off in the headers**, found by measuring the pixels of every screen in both themes. The version beside "Latheport" is now centred on the name (it sat 4 px off), the editor's "Edit" is centred over its tool column (it was 11 px left), and the editor's Text bar no longer has its size slider under the Colour button when several files are open (the editor now also won't shrink narrower than its bar needs). - **Fixed: a password-protected PDF said it was "protected by DRM"** when you chose pages, split or compress. It now says it is password-protected and can't be opened, as everywhere else. PDFs that only have permissions set (open with no password, no editing allowed) are edited, joined, split and compressed, and keep the same permissions (tested). - **Fixed: an RPM, installer or .pkg packed more than 200 to 1 was refused as damaged** (90 MB of zeros in a 90 KB RPM). The limit is now the free space on the drive, as for every other archive. - **Fixed: playing a 3D animation stopped with "Singular matrix"** when a part was scaled down to 0, the usual way to hide one. - **Fixed: a picture of more than 268 million pixels gave a message about "pixport" and `max_pixels=`.** It now says the picture is larger than Latheport opens. - **ConvertAll is now Latheport.** It does more than convert now (an editor, a video timeline, PDF tools, smart tools), and "ConvertAll" was a crowded name. Latheport joins its engines, bookport, pixport, meshport and packport. The program is `Latheport.exe` (and `latheport-cli.exe` in a terminal), with a new icon, a lathe's chuck turning, and the window in its copper instead of indigo (easier to read, too: white on a button went from a contrast of 4.47 to 5.18, past the 4.5 that WCAG asks for). Nothing to set up again: the first time it opens, your settings, presets, watch folders, last formats and update choices come along, downloaded engines and smart tools move over (renamed in place, not downloaded again), and the right-click entries and Start menu shortcut point at Latheport instead. ConvertAll's own settings are left as they were. Entries below 1.5 keep the old name. - **Added: Update now.** When a newer Latheport is out, the banner's **Update now** (with its size) downloads it with progress and *Cancel*, checks it against the SHA-256 GitHub lists, and unpacks it next to your copy; **Restart to update** opens the new version in the same folder, so the right-click menu and Start menu shortcut still point at it. The old copy is kept until the new one has opened, and is put back by itself if it doesn't: checked end to end with the real launcher, both ways. It always jumps to the newest version, however many were skipped. Nothing is downloaded without the click. ConvertAll 1.4's link-only check still finds the release under the new name: tested against a stand-in for GitHub's rename redirect. - **Fixed: `from latheport import plan` failed** (it did in 1.4 too, as `from convertall import plan`). It now gives a conversion's plan without converting, exactly what `--plan --json` prints. - **Added: deep fry.** The meme look for any picture: colours, contrast and sharpness turned way up, grain, and the crunch of a JPG saved over and over. *Deep fry* in the editor is a slider from 1% (a light crisp) to 100% (fried to blocks, the words still readable), or `--deepfry 1` to `100`. Every step up is further from the original (on a test picture, 25 at 1% to 85 at 100%, average difference per pixel out of 255). The picture keeps its size and transparency, animated GIFs are fried frame by frame, and the same picture always fries the same way. It takes 0.15 to 0.3 s for a 1600 x 1200 JPG and about 1.5 s for a 24-megapixel photo. Like a cut, it's for the files at hand: it isn't remembered for the next ones. - **Added: picture effects you'd use every day**, in the editor next to *Deep fry*, or from the command line. Like a cut, they're for the files at hand: they aren't remembered for the next ones. - *Turn* a picture a quarter right or left, upside down, or mirrored (`--rotate right`, `left`, `180`, `mirror`). - *Crop to* a square, 4:5 for posts, 16:9 wide or 9:16 for stories and reels, from the middle (`--crop 4:5`). The check after converting confirms the new width and height. - *Touch up*, *Auto fix colour and contrast* (`--enhance auto`): on a washed-out, blue-tinted test photo, the average difference from the original went from 23.6 to 6.5 (out of 255); a good photo changes by 0.3. - *Touch up*, *Clean up a page* (`--enhance page`) turns a phone photo of a page into white paper and dark writing, in grey. On a test page with a shadow across it, the paper went from 185 ± 32 to an even 255 and the writing from 53 to 27. Use it with PDF for a clean scan in one step. - *Colour*: black and white (a real one-channel grey file, smaller) or sepia (`--colour bw`, `sepia`). - All of them keep transparency and treat every frame of a GIF alike. For a 1600 x 1200 picture each takes under 0.1 s. For a 24-megapixel photo, turning, cropping and colour cost at most 0.1 s more than a plain save (0.15 s), and the touch-ups about 0.9 s in all. - **Added: the editor.** *Edit…* in Options (or the pencil on a dropped picture or video) opens a dark photo-editor window: *Crop*, *Adjust* and *Text* down the left (keys C, A, T), the tool's options along the top, the files in a strip along the bottom. Undo and Redo, Compare (hold it, or `\`), zoom where the pointer is, Space-drag to look around. - *Crop*: drag a box or its corners, or lock it to *Original*, *1:1*, *4:5*, *16:9* or *9:16*; turn and mirror with the box turning along. Guides show as in photo apps: a grid of thirds while the box moves, a line when it's in the middle, edges that snap to the picture's, and a label with the box's size in pixels that names the shape when it is one (*1080 × 1350 · 4:5*). The result is exactly the box chosen, checked after converting. From the command line: `--area 10,5,80,60` (left, top, width, height in percent). - Edits go to all the files, or to one: *All files*, *This file* or *As it is* for the file shown. A crop locked to a shape fits each file's own size (a 4:5 crop of a landscape photo and of a portrait one are both 4:5). - *Turn* can now also mirror and turn together (`--rotate mirror-right`, `mirror-left`, `flip`), so any way a picture lies can be put right. - **Changed: fewer settings in Options.** Turn, Crop to, Touch up, Colour, Deep fry and the watermark moved into the editor; for a photo and a video together Options went from 17 settings to 11. The command line keeps every flag. - **Fixed: Options no longer run off the bottom of the screen.** Opening Options for a video grew the window to fit every setting, past the screen's edge where the last ones couldn't be reached. Now they open in a panel beside the column, under headings (*Picture*, *Video*, *Sound*, *Cut and size*, *Speed*), and the window gets wider, never taller: on a 1080p screen it goes from 460 x 500 to 856 x 500, and back when Options close. What doesn't fit scrolls inside the panel. Switching formats no longer leaves the last format's rows showing over the new ones for a moment. - **Fixed: plain words for a damaged file.** Instead of a library's message with the file's full temporary path ("cannot identify image file 'C:\\Users\\...'"), it says "broken.png doesn't open as a PNG picture: it may be damaged, or not really a PNG". No message shows a full path any more. - **Changed: a newer version shows in a slim banner** under the header, with *See what's new* and *Not now* (that version isn't brought up again), instead of a link squeezed beside the name. - **Fixed: closing Latheport while something was still working in the background could end in a crash report** (a download, an engine install, a check for updates or a 3D model loading): it now closes quietly every time (0 crashes in 12 tries, against 4 to 6 in 10 before). - **Fixed: `latheport --help` stopped with an error** once a setting's description held a percent sign; it prints in full again. - **Fixed: little things a look through every screen found.** Tick boxes showed no box in the light theme; the values in the boxes you can type into sat 5 pixels right of the others; About closed with a different button from the other windows; *Watch folders* with no folders was a blank box (it says what to do now); the editor offered tools for a file it couldn't show. - **Fixed: what a review of the window found** (each with a test that failed before the fix): - Changing a setting with a format other than the suggested one chosen rebuilt every Options row twice, so the field you were typing in lost the keyboard and a slider being dragged was dropped. The rows now stay. - After closing to the notification area once, closing the window never quit Latheport again, even with *Keep watching from the notification area* turned off. It quits again. - The check for updates ran once, 4 s after Latheport opened, and counted as done before it asked: offline at start-up meant no check that day, and a window left open for days never checked again. It now tries again an hour later when GitHub can't be reached, and checks each day while the window stays open. - *Show in folder* picked the wrong file when its name had a comma in it (`a,b.png`). - The dropped picture was made at 240 x 120 pixels and blown up on a 150% or 200% screen; it's made at the screen's own pixels now (480 x 240 at 200%), sharp. - A watched folder's file that stopped or failed was described with the files in the window ("1 saved, 2 not converted" for one file); it's told by its own name now. A watched folder that isn't there (renamed, a drive unplugged) shows as *not there* in *Watch folders*, and from the notification area a file that fails says so in a notification. - The pencil on the dropped file still opened the editor during a conversion (for a PDF the window could freeze until the conversion was done), and each click opened another editor. It waits now, and a second click brings the open one to the front. - A 3D model whose chosen take doesn't move in time (all its keys at one moment) stopped playing with an error on every frame; a minimised window kept playing the drop area's 3D preview unseen. Both fixed. - An XPS page that wasn't readable came out as a raw "ParseError" for any page but the first (it says which page is damaged now), and each page was read twice (the first three times). - *Details* printed the editor's settings as stored (a crop as "10,5,80,60", texts and drawings as code); it says them in words now ("cropped, 1 text, black and white"). - **Fixed: what a review of the conversions found** (each with a test that failed before the fix): - *Update now* failed whenever Latheport had been opened from its Start menu shortcut or by a double-click: those run it in its own folder, and Windows won't rename a folder a running program is in, so the swap gave up after 30 s and said the update had failed. The update helper now leaves that folder first, and the new version runs in its own. What earlier updates left (the old copy and a version that didn't start, about 230 MB each, and the helper's folder in %TEMP%) is now removed, also beside an app folder with [ ] in its name. Only folders an update moved aside are removed: a folder of your own named `Latheport.old` or `Latheport.failed` (a backup, say) is never deleted, and if one is in the way the update stops and says so instead. - A YAML file of 281 bytes whose aliases nest six deep (each naming the one before ten times) became 13 MB of JSON, and three more levels would have been 13 GB, written where Cancel can't stop it. It's refused with how many values it would expand to (12,345,685); ordinary anchors and `<<:` merges work as before. - Speech recognition let FFmpeg follow web addresses inside a file (an .mp3 that's really a playlist). It reads local files only, as every other FFmpeg step does. - *Upscale* 2x filled a 4x picture of float numbers first: about 50 times the result's size in memory (370 MB for a 0.6-megapixel photo; a 20-megapixel one, inside the limit, would have asked for gigabytes). It now keeps 3 bytes a pixel of the result: 21 MB for the same photo, the same picture (4x is byte for byte the same, 2x within 2 levels on 0.2% of values). - An animated GIF, WebP or PNG gave every frame the first frame's time (100, 2000 and 100 ms became 100, 100 and 100). Each frame keeps its own. - `notes.txt.gz` to XZ was named `notes.txt.gz.xz` (and extracted to a text file named `notes.txt.gz`); it's `notes.txt.xz`. - A CSV, JSON or spreadsheet result between 50 and 200 MB was reported as "doesn't open"; it's just not checked again, as other big files aren't. - Pictures and subtitles laid over a video failed when a folder in the way had an apostrophe in its name ("Bob's files"), which the temp folder has when the Windows user name does. - *Cancel* now stops inside long steps, not only between them: between the pages of a PDF made into pictures or text and of a comic, between the tiles of an upscale, and a megabyte at a time inside a big file in a TAR archive. Before, a 1,000-page PDF drew every page first. - Columns with the same name in a CSV or spreadsheet overwrote each other (`name,value,value` kept only the second value); the second is now "value 2". XML text after a child element (`

Hello world again

`) was dropped. Converting to TOML or plist now says that empty (null) values are left out. - An engine that ran too long ended with its whole command line ("Command '[...soffice.com', '--headless'...]' timed out after 600 seconds"); it says "soffice took longer than 10 minutes, so it was stopped". - A text file in UTF-16 without a byte order mark (some Excel and Windows exports) came out full of empty characters; it's read as UTF-16. - An email or Outlook message saved as HTML kept the mail's `on...=` scripts, `javascript:` links and pictures from the web (a sender's tracking pixel tells them it was opened); they're taken out, and the mail's own pictures and links stay. Pictures a mail's own style asked for from the web (`background:url(https://...)`, `@import`) and links split to dodge the check (`javascript:`) are taken out too. An MHT web archive whose part was named `a.png` also rewrote the address `a.png.bak`, and the pictures its stylesheets load were left out; both fixed. - Two programs finishing a file of the same name into one folder at the same moment (the window and `latheport watch`) could overwrite one result with the other; the second now gets `name (1)`. - `--plan` could show a different route than the conversion takes (one needing an engine that isn't installed), and a bad setting given to `plan()` raised a ValueError instead of saying what's wrong. - An error message naming two files ("Couldn't rename C:\...\b.txt to C:\...\d.txt") came out as "Couldn't rename d.txt"; each path is cut to its own name. - A file left half written when an archive entry turned out damaged, too big or cancelled part-way is now removed. - A linear-light picture (an XCF in linear precision, an EXR) made into a JPEG kept its own colour profile though it was given the sRGB curve, so viewers showed it far too bright; the profile is left out for those now. - A different page or file count in the check after converting was put down to whatever the conversion noted first, even a note about something else; only a note about that count explains it now. - **Added: the keyboard can do it all in the window.** Ctrl+O chooses files (or Tab to the drop area and press Enter), Ctrl+Enter converts, Esc cancels. In the editor, Ctrl+V pastes into a text. - **Fixed: the editor, before its first release.** Dragging the text *Size* slider made an Undo step for every value it passed (28 for one drag, pushing older steps out of the 100 kept); it's one step now, and the slider keeps the keyboard. Left, Right, Page Up and Page Down while typing a text switched to another file; they stay in the text. Closing the editor or the Pages window with work still running waited 3 s for each job in turn (12 s frozen with four), and could end Latheport with a crash report when that work went on after the window closed, or was still going when Latheport quit; it waits 3 s for all of them together now, and lets them finish safely. FFmpeg missing while a video was paused left the rough frame up with no word. The *Done* button turned lavender under the mouse instead of a lighter copper. - **Faster in the editor:** with a see-through picture zoomed in 8 times, each redraw (every caret blink and every move of a drag) took 1.15 s; it takes 0.015 s (the checkerboard is one fill of what's on the screen, and texts and drawings are made at the picture's own pixels, not 8 times them). Dragging a text at that zoom: 1.9 s a move, now 0.21 s. At the fitted size a redraw takes 5 ms instead of 10, the picture identical. Video frames are copied once on their way to the screen instead of twice (4.0 ms a 1080p frame, now 2.0). A watermark's corner is checked without copying the whole photo first (61 ms on a 24-megapixel photo, now 18). - **Changed: no title bar.** The window's own header is its title bar now, with the version beside the name; drag it to move the window, double-click to maximise. Windows still snaps it to the screen's edges, shows Windows 11's snap layouts over the maximise button, resizes it from every edge and gives it its shadow. Every other window has its own title bar too: the editor, the 3D viewer, *Engines*, *Watch folders*, *Conversion details*, *About*, the colour picker, and every question and message, which now answer in plain words (*Stop and close*, *Keep converting*). Small windows can't be maximised or stretched by their edges; the viewer, *Watch folders* and *Details* can. - **Added: text on pictures and videos.** In the editor, *Text* works as in Photoshop: click anywhere on the picture and type there, with the cursor where the next letter goes. The bar at the top sets the font (Sans, Serif, Bold or Handwriting), size, colour and an outline or a shadow, for the next text or for the one clicked. Click a text to type in it or drag it; Enter or Esc when done; any number of texts. *Meme* adds big upper-case captions at the top and bottom, white with a black outline; long ones wrap onto up to three lines and stay inside the picture. From the command line: `--text "..."`, again for more, with `--text-at top|middle|bottom` and `--text-style meme`. The four fonts come with Latheport (976 KB, all under the SIL Open Font License), so text looks the same on every PC. - **Added: a watermark**, your own text small in a corner, see-through, dark where the corner is bright so it always shows (`--watermark "my-site.example"`, `--watermark-at`). There is none unless you type one, and once typed it's remembered. - **Added: video effects.** *Turn*, *Crop to* (or by hand), *Colour* (black and white, sepia), text and the watermark work on videos, GIFs and animated WebP too. A phone video saved upright with a rotation tag is cropped as you see it. On a 20 s 1080p clip, a plain conversion takes 3.5 s; turned 3.8 s, cropped square 2.5 s, black and white 3.3 s, two texts and a watermark 3.9 s. - **Added: speed and backwards for sound and video.** *Speed* from 0.25x to 4x: voices keep their pitch (a 440 Hz test tone stays at 440 Hz at 2x), or set *Pitch* to change with it, like a tape (880 Hz at 2x). The length is checked afterwards (8 s at 2x: 4.0 s). *Backwards* plays it in reverse frame for frame, sound included, a few seconds at a time so it needs little memory: a 40 s 1080p video in 10.4 s, exactly its 1,200 frames. It takes up to 10 minutes. Speed and Backwards are for the files at hand; Pitch is remembered. - Text and watermarks add little time: on a 24-megapixel photo, 0.31 s for two meme captions and 0.36 s for a watermark, against 0.15 s for a plain save (0.04 s each on a 1600 x 1200 picture). - **Added: Adjust, in the editor.** Sliders for brightness, contrast, saturation, warmth and sharpness (-100 to 100), shown on the picture as you move them, or `--adjust brightness=15,warmth=20`. Each moves the picture its way: on a test photo, brightness +50 took its average from 151 to 173 (and -50 to 124), contrast +50 its spread from 47 to 63, saturation -100 its colour to none. Videos get the same through FFmpeg, within 1.5 to 3.5 levels (out of 255) of what the editor shows. A 24-megapixel photo takes 0.65 s with all five, against 0.13 s for a plain save; a 20 s 1080p video 4.1 s against 2.6 s. - **Added: Straighten.** Turn a crooked horizon level, up to 15 degrees either way in tenths, with a grid over the picture while you drag; it's cut in just enough that no corner is empty, and keeps its size (`--straighten -2.5`). Pictures and videos alike: 1.1 s for a 24-megapixel photo (0.13 s plain), 4.0 s for a 20 s 1080p video (2.6 s plain). - **Added: Hide.** In the editor, drag a box over a face, a number plate or a password and choose *Pixelate*, *Blur* or *Cover* (solid black, the safe way to hide text), with a strength slider; or `--hide pixelate:40,55,12,8` (again for more). Not a pixel outside the box changes (tested on pictures pixel for pixel). It works on every kind of picture and on every frame of a video, and costs almost nothing: 0.17 s for three boxes on a 24-megapixel photo (0.13 s plain), 2.7 s on a 20 s 1080p video (2.6 s plain). - **Added: Draw.** Arrows, lines, boxes and ellipses (Shift for 45 degrees and squares), the pen, a see-through highlighter, and stickers: a tick, a cross, a star, a heart and numbers that count up as you put them down. Colour, width and fill are in the panel; *Select* picks a drawing up to move or delete it. Drawings are placed on the picture itself, so they stay on what they point at when the crop changes, and they turn with it. Ten drawings take 0.39 s on a 24-megapixel photo and 2.9 s on a 20 s 1080p video (2.6 s plain). - **Added: a picture as the watermark, and an opacity for it.** Your logo (a PNG with a see-through background works best), your text or both, small in a corner, as solid as the *Opacity* slider says (5 to 100%: at 40% it's drawn at exactly 40%). Kept for next time like the text one (`--watermark-image logo.png --watermark-opacity 40`). If the picture is moved or deleted, the conversion says so in plain words instead of leaving it out unnoticed. - **Added: videos play in the editor, with a timeline to trim them.** Space plays and pauses with the sound, comma and period step one frame (exactly: 1/25 s on a 25 fps video), and a strip of pictures under the stage shows the whole video; click or drag on it to go anywhere. Drag either end of the strip to keep just a part, or press I and O where you are. The new *Trim* tool (V) sets the speed (0.25x to 4x, pitch kept or changing) and backwards, and saves the frame shown as a picture next to the video with every edit on it, in 0.14 s for a 720p frame. Trims and speed are each video's own, so trimming one clip doesn't trim the others. Playback is [puretech-player](https://github.com/puretechteam/puretech-player): the first frame shows 71 ms after you press play, a seek lands on the exact frame, and the picture strip for a 6 s 720p video is ready in 0.17 s. Videos play with the FFmpeg Latheport installs and with one from Chocolatey too (gyan.dev's essentials build, which has no AV1 decoder: checked on a GitHub runner, every frame shown). - **Added: a paused video shows exactly what the conversion makes.** While a video plays the editor shows it turned, cropped, drawn on and in black and white; paused or moved, FFmpeg makes the frame with every effect through the conversion's own filters (80 ms for a 720p frame), so what you see is what you get. Compared with FFmpeg's own frame at that moment, the editor's picture differs by under 2 levels out of 255. - **Added: PDF tools.** A PDF can be converted to a PDF to change its pages: - *Edit…* opens the **Pages** window: every page as a picture, to drag into another order, turn or take out, with Undo; the pages picked can be saved as a PDF of their own. From the command line: `--pages 3,1-2,5r`. - **Join** PDFs (tick *Join*): their pages one after another in one PDF, with every bookmark; in the Pages window they show as one grid, to merge and order at once. - **Split into** PDFs of any number of pages, together in a folder (`--split 1` for one PDF per page), each named for its pages and carrying the bookmarks of its own pages. - **Compress**: *Smaller* (pictures at 150 dpi) or *Balanced* (200 dpi), text staying text. A 4-page 300 dpi scan of 3.11 MB became 0.67 MB (Smaller) or 1.27 MB (Balanced), and drawn at 150 dpi the worst page kept a PSNR of 34.5 and 35.7 dB. - Bookmarks follow their pages (those for pages taken out go) and the title, links and form fields stay: on an 85-page book, keeping 49 pages in a new order kept its three remaining chapters pointing at the right pages. The check after converting counts the pages (85 across 5 split parts: the same). Protected PDFs are left as they are, said in words. All of it is bookport's, which reads and writes PDFs itself; PDFium only draws the pages in the window. - **Added: smart tools**, each run on this computer (nothing is sent anywhere) and downloaded once the first time it's needed, asked first with its size: the window offers it as it does FFmpeg, the command line asks or takes `-y`. Each download is pinned and checked against its SHA-256, and it's kept whole or not at all. ONNX Runtime comes with the first one (15 MB). They keep to three quarters of the cores, so the computer stays usable. - **Background** (190 MB): *Taken out* (see-through), *White*, *Black* or *Blurred* like a phone's portrait mode, in the editor's *Adjust* panel with the result shown, or `--background remove`. BiRefNet finds the subject. On 15 test pictures with things in the background touching the subject, it found it with an IoU of 0.988 or more (0.994 on average); IS-Net, the other model tried, took in part of the background on 7 of them (IoU 0.75 to 0.87). The edges are then fitted to the picture's own (28% less error at the edges on 12 test pictures), and their colour freed of the old background, so no fringe shows on a new one. On a 16-thread PC a 2-megapixel photo takes 5.8 s and a 12-megapixel one 8.5 s, the model's loading included, with at most 2.0 GB of memory in use. - **Upscale** 2x or 4x (5 MB): Real-ESRGAN draws in sharp edges where resizing blurs (`--upscale 2`). On text made 4x smaller and back, it came out 0.8 dB closer to the original than bicubic resizing at 4x and 4.6 dB at 2x. On soft, blurred photos it sharpens what was soft, so plain resizing measures closer there. It works in tiles, so memory stays flat for any size, and no seams show where they meet. A 640 x 480 picture takes 3.7 s at 2x and 10.4 s at 4x (most of that saving the 4.9-megapixel PNG), with 290 MB of memory. - **Picture to text** (OCR, 10 MB): any picture, or every page of a TIFF scan, becomes a text file. PaddleOCR's models read Latin letters (English, French, German, Spanish and 28 more). On 10 test pages in two fonts, sizes from 14 to 44 pixels, blurred and tilted 2 degrees, 1.2% of characters came out wrong; a tilted page is read levelled. *Copy the text in it* in the editor puts a picture's text on the clipboard. An A4 page at 300 dpi takes 1.8 s; a page of 11-point text came out without a single mistake. - **Make searchable**, for PDFs (`--searchable yes`): scanned pages are read and their words laid over them unseen, each on its own word, so the PDF can be searched and its text copied, also on pages stored turned. On a test scan, a word found by PDFium lay within 3 points of where the picture has it. Pages with text of their own stay as they are. Five scanned A4 pages take 16 s, 3.2 s a page. - **Speech to subtitles and text** (Whisper, 80 MB): sound and video become SRT, VTT, ASS (and the other subtitle formats) or a transcript (`latheport talk.mp3 --to srt`). From a video, choose *Subtitles from: What's said* (`--subtitles-from speech`); or add them to a video, *Burned into the picture* (in the Inter font, sized for the picture) or *As a subtitle track* in MP4, MKV, MOV or WebM (`--speech-subs burn`). Cut and speed are followed. The language is heard in the first 30 seconds or set (`--language fr`, 99 languages). Subtitles are at most two lines of 42 characters, and silence is skipped (Whisper writes "you" over it otherwise). On speech made with Windows' own voice, every word came out right but for numbers written as figures ("9" for "nine"). 33 s of speech takes 2.6 s and 3 min 16 s takes 18 s, about 11 times as fast as it plays, with 540 MB of memory. - **Fixed: sound to subtitles failed.** MP3 to SRT (and any sound to subtitles) went through an MKA to take out a subtitle track a sound file can't have, and failed every time. It's speech recognition now. A video with no subtitle track says how to write down what's said instead. - **Changed: no "TXT is lossy" or "see-through" note when a picture's text or a recording's speech becomes text or subtitles**: they don't apply to words. - **Added: pictures can be saved as their own format** (JPG to JPG, PNG to PNG), to turn, crop, touch up, fry, shrink or change the quality of a picture without changing what it is. The original is never replaced: the result gets a new name next to it. - **No Ghostscript needed.** PostScript and EPS are now read and written by Latheport itself (through [bookport](https://github.com/puretechteam/bookport)), so there's nothing to download first and nothing to keep up to date. The engines left are FFmpeg and LibreOffice, and gmsh for CAD parts. - *EPS and PS to PDF* (and on to pictures, SVG and DXF): compared with Ghostscript on 25 files (charts from matplotlib, LibreOffice drawings, pictures, Ghostscript's own PostScript, a 60-page document), every page looks the same to within an SSIM of 0.99, 9 of the files pixel for pixel. Text stays text you can search and copy, in the file's own fonts. A chart takes a few hundredths of a second. - *PDF to EPS and PS*: the PDF's fonts go in, and every word comes back out when the PostScript is opened again. Against Ghostscript, a page of photos is 6 times smaller (2.4 MB against 15.5 MB) and a LibreOffice page 8 times faster to write. A page with see-through parts, which PostScript can't have, goes in as a 300 dpi picture of the page. - A PostScript file is a program, and it runs in a sandbox now: it can't open, run or delete other files, and one that runs too long is stopped.

releases.name: ConvertAll 1.4.0
releases.body:
**Download:** `ConvertAll-1.4.0-windows.zip` below. Unzip it and run `ConvertAll\ConvertAll.exe`. Nothing to install. Keep `ConvertAll.exe` next to its `_internal` folder.

### 2026-11-05: ConvertAll 1.4.0, no ImageMagick, Pandoc or DjVuLibre needed, cut, fit and join sound and video, watch folders

- **No ImageMagick, Pandoc or DjVuLibre needed.** Camera RAW, GIMP, EXR, HDR and JPEG XL pictures go through [pixport](https://github.com/puretechteam/pixport), new and ours; markup languages and DjVu books through [bookport](https://github.com/puretechteam/bookport). That's about 330 MB of installs no one needs any more: of 13,027 conversions, 8,725 now work with no engine at all (7,431 of 12,506 in 1.3.0), and none needs one of those three. FFmpeg, LibreOffice and Ghostscript are the engines left. Measured against 1.3.0 with the engines, same files, same PC:
  - **Camera RAW to PNG:** 12 photos in 59.0 s instead of 91.7 s (old and new taking turns on each file, best of 3, as for the times below), and 2% smaller PNGs. Colours as LibRaw gives them (median ΔE2000 2.08 on 76 photos from 11 makers).
  - **EXR, HDR, XCF and JPEG XL to PNG:** HDR 2.3 times (16 files, 12.4 s instead of 28.2 s), JPEG XL 1.6 times (27, 21 of them faster), XCF 1.6 times (28, 22 of them faster) and EXR 1.3 times (71, 19.3 s instead of 25.7 s; 48 are faster and the others within 0.4 s) as fast. An HDR picture's PNG now shows the right brightness in every viewer (ImageMagick's looked dark outside a few), and keeps 16 bits a channel, which takes more room: 51 MB against 39 MB for HDR, 92.5 MB against 71 MB for EXR. The new *Colour depth* setting makes them 18 MB and 26.5 MB. A multi-part EXR keeps its whole picture (its display window), not just the part with data. ImageMagick's own PNGs packed again by pixport come out 8.8% smaller (109 of 112).
  - **JPG to JPEG XL** keeps the photo exactly as it is, 17% smaller (median of 22 photos), and can be turned back into the identical JPG. ImageMagick encoded it again, losing a little.
  - **Markup languages:** to HTML 5.7 times, to Markdown 4.5 times and to Word 2.3 times as fast as Pandoc on 45 conversions of LaTeX, reStructuredText, Org, AsciiDoc and MediaWiki files. New: Typst, DocBook, man pages and Textile, equations (into Word's own equations too), BibTeX citations, and Markdown or HTML to Word and OpenDocument without LibreOffice. All 1,333 markup files of our test collection read, none slower than 0.47 s.
  - **DjVu to PDF:** 28.9 s instead of 388.8 s for 20 books, 146 MB instead of 2,194 MB, closer to the original pages than DjVuLibre's own PDFs (median 48.4 dB against 36.5 dB on 59 pages), and the PDF is searchable (its OCR text comes along); DjVu to text 6.4 times as fast.
- **Checked: RAW, GIMP, EXR, HDR and JPEG XL results.** Their picture size, transparency and photo info are compared before and after, like every other picture's.
- **Added: cut sound and video.** *Start at* and *End at* in the Options card (or `--start 1:30 --end 5:00`) keep just that part, in seconds, `m:ss` or `h:mm:ss`. A file can now be converted to its own format (MP4 to MP4, WAV to WAV) to cut it, shrink it or even out its loudness. The result's length is checked: in our tests a 4.5 s cut from a 12 s video came out 4.5 s long, within 0.06 s. A cut is for the files it was set on: it isn't remembered for the next ones, nor saved in presets.
- **Added: fit a video or a song in a size.** *Fit in* (`--target-size 10`) takes megabytes, with 10 MB for Discord and 25 MB for email in the list. ConvertAll works out the bitrate from the length and encodes in two passes (MP4, MKV, MOV, WebM and the other H.264 and VP9 formats), scaling the picture down when it would otherwise turn to mush. A 60 s 720p video asked to fit in 10 MB came out at 9.66 MB in 6.7 s; a video that already looks right at a smaller size isn't padded out. The size is checked after converting.
- **Added: even out loudness.** *Loudness* (`--loudness streaming` or `broadcast`) brings sound to -14 LUFS, as streaming services play it, or -23 LUFS for TV (EBU R128, measured first, then set in a second pass). The result is measured afterwards: a quiet 20 s recording came out at -14.0 and -23.0 LUFS.
- **Added: watch folders.** ☰ → *Watch folders…*: files that land in a folder you pick are converted to the format you pick, into a `Converted` folder inside it, once they've finished arriving (a file that is still growing or that another program is still writing, such as a big copy, a browser's `.crdownload` or `.part`, and Office's lock files are left until they're whole). Originals are never touched, and files already there are left alone. It works while the window is open, or from the notification area after closing it if you tick that. `convertall watch FOLDER --to FORMAT` does the same from a terminal until Ctrl+C.
- **Added: files dropped while converting wait their turn** in a list under the window, instead of being ignored: waiting, converting, saved or didn't convert, each with its file and target. Select a waiting one and press Delete (or right-click) to take it out. *Cancel* stops what's waiting too.
- **Added: a once-a-day update check.** When a newer ConvertAll is out, the window shows a link to it at the top. It's one request to GitHub, sends nothing about you or your files, downloads nothing, and can be turned off in ☰ → *Check for updates once a day*.
- **Added: join sound or videos into one.** Drop several and tick *Join them into one file, in this order* (or `--join`): videos are fitted into the first one's picture size and frame rate, videos without sound get silence, and the result's length is checked against the parts added up.
- **Added: Colour depth.** PNG and TIFF from RAW, EXR, HDR and XCF pictures can be 8 bits a channel (*Colour depth* in the Options card, or `--bit-depth 8`), about a third of the size: 16 HDR files came to 18 MB instead of 51 MB. They stay at as many bits as the picture has unless you choose.
- **Changed: the download is smaller.** 77.0 MB instead of 1.3.0's 81.7 MB, without Python code and plugins no conversion uses.
- **Fixed: a crash window from `convertall-cli` in scripts.** With no one to answer "install this engine?" (input from NUL, as scheduled tasks and many scripts have), the terminal tool showed a crash window and waited until someone closed it. It now says to re-run with `-y` and exits, and any unexpected error goes to the terminal instead of a window. Also in 1.3.0.
- **Fixed: very detailed big pictures to HEIC.** Past about 16 MB of picture data (a 24-megapixel Fujifilm RAW at the usual quality came to 17.5 MB), the result opened in FFmpeg but not in many HEIC readers, ConvertAll's own included. The quality now steps down until it opens (85 instead of 90 on that photo, 16.7 MB), and the result says so.
- **Fixed: fine sound to WMA, WMV, ASF, OGG and OGV.** WMA failed from 96 kHz up, and Vorbis on DSD, which leaves FFmpeg at 352.8 kHz, so DSD to OGG or WMA never worked. Such sound is now brought down to 48 or 192 kHz, and the result says so.
- **Fixed: a crash code when closing the window while something was still working in the background** (a thumbnail, a 3D preview loading, an engine installing, the update check). ConvertAll ended with error 0xC0000409 in 13 of 13 tries, and now closes normally in 13 of 13, with settings saved. Also in 1.3.0, apart from the update check, which is new.
- **Fixed: the same conversion could go a different way each time.** When two routes tied, the choice changed from one run to the next: 2,147 of the 13,027 routes differed across 4 runs, some through a JPG on the way (a video to EXR, say) and some not. Each route is now the same on every run, and a tie never goes through a JPG. Also in 1.3.0.
- **Fixed: Cancel on a busy PC.** Stopping an engine took 1.5 s with 350 programs running, because it waited on Windows' `taskkill`. ConvertAll now ends the engine and what it started itself.
- **Fixed: 3D to DAE in the download.** Every conversion to DAE failed with a missing `schema-1.4.1.xml`, because that file wasn't packed. It worked only from source. Also in 1.3.0.

releases.name: ConvertAll 1.3.0
releases.body:
**Download:** `ConvertAll-1.3.0-windows.zip` below. Unzip it and run `ConvertAll\ConvertAll.exe`. Nothing to install. Keep `ConvertAll.exe` next to its `_internal` folder.

### 2026-11-01: ConvertAll 1.3.0, no 7-Zip needed, half the download, Cancel and a safe close

- **Changed: 7-Zip is no longer needed.** Every archive, disc and disk image ConvertAll used to hand to 7-Zip is now read by [packport](https://github.com/puretechteam/packport) 0.3.1, with its compiled decoders (packport-native) built in: RAR and CBR (RAR 4 and 5, compressed, solid, split into volumes), CAB, ISO, UDF, WIM, LZH, ARJ, squashfs, deb, RPM, xar and pkg, the ZIP and 7z files Python's own readers can't open (Deflate64, PPMd, BCJ2, damaged ones), and disk images: VHD, VHDX, VMDK, QCOW2, VDI and DMG, with the FAT, NTFS, ext, HFS+ and APFS file systems on them. CHM and LIT come out through bookport, MSI and MSP through ConvertAll itself. Ghostscript, when ConvertAll installs it, is unpacked from its installer by packport too (the same 4 files, byte for byte). 7-Zip is gone from ☰ → *Engines…* and `convertall engines`, and an installed 7-Zip is no longer used. Before: 350 conversion steps and 29 kinds of archive needed 7-Zip; now none do.
  - **About as fast as with 7-Zip.** `convertall --extract` from the command line, ConvertAll 1.2.0 (with 7-Zip 24.09) against 1.3.0, same files, best of 3: a 58 MB CBR of 40 JPEG pages in 0.47 s instead of 0.49 s, and to PDF in 0.60 s instead of 0.86 s (1.4 times as fast); a RAR 4 that unpacks to 242 MB in 0.58 s instead of 0.59 s; a small RAR 5 in 0.41 s instead of 0.42 s; a UDF disc and a WIM in the same time (0.48 s and 0.50 s). Slower: an LZX CAB (0.55 s instead of 0.50 s), and 7z files packed with PPMd (1.38 s instead of 1.10 s) or BCJ2 (1.08 s instead of 0.80 s), where 7-Zip's own decoders are faster. squashfs, VHDX and DMG files that 1.2.0 failed on (7-Zip stopped at their links) now unpack. py7zr stays as the first reader for 7z: packport is faster on some 7z files and slower on others. packport goes on reading everything without the compiled decoders, only more slowly, where they aren't there (`convertall engines` says which is in use).
  - **Layouts.** A disk image gives the files on it, a folder per partition (`1 NTFS`, `2 FAT32`), where 7-Zip gave the partitions as images. An MSI gives its streams under their real names, with the CAB inside unpacked into a folder. A deb comes out as `dpkg-deb -R` lays it out, an RPM as `rpm2cpio` does, a pkg with its Payload unpacked. ISO discs keep their full Rock Ridge names (7-Zip cut long names short, so files with the same first 64 characters were lost).
  - **Refused, with a message:** password-protected archives, BitLocker (To Go too), LUKS, LVM, encrypted DMGs and APFS volumes. **Not read yet:** DMGs and files compressed with LZFSE (`ULFO` DMGs), exFAT, classic HFS, WIM's LZMS (`.esd`).
  - **Tested:** the archive tests now run without 7-Zip, and fail if anything starts it. The safety tests (escaping names, Windows names, duplicates, links, passwords, cut-short archives, bombs) run through packport, and every one of the 907 conversions from an archive or comic format passes (679 before, with 228 skipped for want of a sample of CAB, LZH, ARJ, MSI, UDF, disk images and the rest, which now have one).
- **Changed: the download is less than half the size.** The zip is 81.7 MB instead of 1.2.0's 179.1 MB (54% smaller), and 182.5 MB unpacked instead of 393.4 MB:
  - PDFs are read and drawn by PDFium, Chrome's PDF engine (7.4 MB), instead of PyMuPDF (37.7 MB): see below.
  - gmsh, the 85 MB engine that turns STEP, IGES and BREP parts into meshes, is downloaded the first time a CAD part needs it (a 42 MB download from PyPI, checked against its published SHA-256), the way LibreOffice and FFmpeg are installed. The window offers it; `convertall engines --install gmsh` too.
  - `convertall-cli.exe` is a 336 KB launcher (`packaging/launcher`, in Rust, needing no Visual C++ runtime) that runs `ConvertAll.exe` in its terminal mode, where it was a 22.8 MB copy of all of ConvertAll's code. Output, exit codes, `--json` and Ctrl+C work as before; `convertall-cli --version` takes 0.37 s instead of 0.33 s.
  - scipy and its own copy of OpenBLAS (about 60 MB) are left out: only trimesh brought them, for things ConvertAll doesn't use. Every 3D sample converts to every mesh format to the same bytes without them.
  - bookport's fonts take 0.86 MB instead of 2.4 MB, with the PDFs it writes unchanged byte for byte.
- **Changed: PDF, XPS and SVG without PyMuPDF.** PyMuPDF is licensed under the AGPL; what ConvertAll used it for is now done by permissively licensed parts and ConvertAll's own code:
  - PDF and Illustrator pages to pictures, PDF to text, page counts, thumbnails and comics out of PDFs (scanned pages still come out byte for byte): PDFium.
  - PDF to SVG (text as outlines) and PDF to DXF read the page's shapes through PDFium. Drawn back, a sample page's SVG differs from MuPDF's own picture of it by 0.02 on a 0-255 scale.
  - XPS and OpenXPS to PDF: drawn with Qt from the document's pages, paths, pictures and embedded (de-obfuscated) fonts, with the text kept searchable. Pages match MuPDF's pictures of them within 0.3 to 0.56 on a 0-255 scale, and the text reads back the same.
  - SVG to PDF and pictures, and DXF drawings to PDF and PNG (through ezdxf's SVG): Qt. As with MuPDF, an SVG can't pull a picture from elsewhere on the computer into its result (Qt on its own loads one by any path, or relative to the working folder): only pictures carried inside the SVG are drawn, and the tests check absolute paths, `file:` links, `../` paths, XML entities and CSS `@import`.
  - A PDF page is drawn with at most 150 million pixels (an A4 or Letter page at 1200 dpi, the highest setting): a 200-inch page at 150 dpi would have taken 900 million (3.6 GB) and is now drawn smaller.
  - HTML and text to PDF: laid out by bookport, with the page size and text size settings.
- **Added: a licenses folder in the download.** The zip now holds ConvertAll's `LICENSE.txt` and a `licenses` folder with the license of each of the 60 components inside it, the GPL and LGPL texts they refer to, and where each one's source is. One of them, x265 (inside pillow-heif, for saving HEIC), is GPL-licensed, so the download as a whole is distributed under the GPL's terms; ConvertAll's own code stays MIT. `packaging/release.py` won't make a zip if a bundled component has no license text.
- **Fixed: Ctrl+C in the terminal** stopped the program wherever it was: in our test it crashed in the middle of a 100 MB extraction (an access violation), or left its temporary folder behind. It now stops the conversion the way *Cancel* does in the window, at its next safe point with nothing half-written, says so and exits with code 130. A second Ctrl+C stops at once.
- **Fixed: every DXF conversion failed in the Windows app** (*"No module named 'unittest'"*), in 1.2.0 too: DXF to SVG, PDF and PNG, and PDF or SVG to DXF. The build left out Python's `unittest`, which pyparsing (under ezdxf) loads. It's back, and a test now imports every library the conversions use with what the build leaves out blocked, as in the app.
- **Fixed: cancelling a PPMd 7z crashed ConvertAll.** py7zr's PPMd decoder crashes when it's freed part-way through a file, which is what *Cancel* (and closing the window mid-extraction) does. PPMd 7z and CB7 files are now read by packport, which stops cleanly.
- **Fixed: a cut-short Windows Installer file** gave Python's own error (*"bytes length not a multiple of item size"*); it now says the package is damaged. Messages about damaged archives no longer mention packport, which ConvertAll's users have never heard of: *"ConvertAll doesn't know what kind of archive this is; it may be damaged"*. Checked on 1,950 damaged copies of ConvertAll's 78 sample archives: every one ends in a clear message, none in a crash, and none leaves anything behind.
- **Changed: ebooks ([bookport](https://github.com/puretechteam/bookport) 0.2.0).** Python's documentation CHM becomes an EPUB in 19.5 s instead of 27.1 s, with 0 epubcheck errors instead of 329. Text in PDFs is kerned (AV, To and the rest spaced as the font says). A correct PDF no longer gets a false amber *Words* warning: lines with numbers in them were dropped when counting, so a 144,227-word book counted as 137,927. Plucker books keep their pictures. CHM and LIT files can be extracted (the same 555 files as 7-Zip gave, for Python's documentation).
- **Changed: 3D ([meshport](https://github.com/puretechteam/meshport) 0.4.0).** Blender files come out closer to what Blender shows: Array caps, subdivided UVs and creases, F-curve modifiers such as Cycles, and exponential and elastic easing. Lights in .blend and glTF files are kept between them. USD meshes with animated points play.
- **Added: more results are checked.** RAR, CBR, CPIO, ISO and WIM results are now opened and counted after converting, like ZIP, 7z and tar: 8,766 of the 12,506 conversions have their result checked (7,682 before).
- **Fixed: archives without an extension** (a download saved as `file`, say) are recognized by what's in them: squashfs, UDF, APFS and HFS+ images, deb and macOS pkg packages and Windows Installer files were missed before (read as a plain ar or xar archive, a Word file, or not at all). All 22 kinds of archive and disk image tried are recognized now; 15 were before.
- **Changed: extracting only the first piece of a split archive** (a `.001` with no `.002` beside it) now says to put the other pieces in the same folder, instead of only saying the archive is damaged.
- **Fixed: files dated before 1980 stopped a ZIP** (*"ZIP does not support timestamps before 1980"*), for example when repacking an old RPM or tar. They get ZIP's first date, 1980, as other ZIP tools give them.
- **Added: big archives say how far they've got.** Extracting one over 50 MB shows the megabytes written so far in the status line (*Extracting · big.rar · 123 of 640 MB*).
- **Added: Cancel.** While a conversion runs, the *Convert* button becomes *Cancel*. It stops the engine at once (FFmpeg, LibreOffice and the rest, with anything they started; measured within 1 s), writes nothing half-made, and keeps the files already done (*Stopped*, with *1 saved, 2 not converted* under it). *Cancel* looks like an ordinary button, so it doesn't pass for *Convert*, and the second click of a double-click on *Convert* doesn't cancel what the first one started.
- **Fixed: closing the window during a conversion.** ConvertAll used to quit with an error (exit code 127 in 10 of 10 tries) and leave the engine running in the background. Now it asks *Stop converting and close?* (or just closes, if the conversion finished while it asked), stops the engine and closes cleanly: exit code 0 in 10 of 10, no engine left running, no temporary folder left behind.
- **Changed: converting with the check is faster.** The original is read once, for the check and the conversion, instead of twice. A 24-megapixel TIFF to PNG takes 3.91 s instead of 4.35 s (10% faster), MOBI to EPUB 0.30 s instead of 0.41 s (26%), FB2 to EPUB and a rigged GLB to STL about 8% faster. The results are the same.
- **Fixed: text files saved as "Unicode" in Notepad (UTF-16).** Subtitles (SRT, VTT, ASS and the rest) came out garbled; GeoJSON maps and Jupyter notebooks failed to open, also when saved in the old Windows encoding. All of them are read correctly now.
- **Fixed: animations made into AVIF or WebP** (a video or GIF turned into an animated picture) got a false warning, *Length: 2.1 s → 0*. The check now reads how long those animations really run.
- **Fixed: PDF to Markdown, LaTeX, reStructuredText, Org, AsciiDoc and MediaWiki came out empty.** LibreOffice opens a PDF as positioned text boxes, which Pandoc skipped on that route. These now go through Word (DOCX), where Pandoc reads them, and keep the text of every page.
- **Fixed: very small pictures (under 18 pixels a side) made into OGV** gave a video no player could open. They are now enlarged to 18 pixels, keeping their shape, and the report says so.
- **Changed: a conversion waiting for LibreOffice** (while another ConvertAll window uses it) can be cancelled, and gives up after 15 minutes with a message instead of waiting forever.

releases.name: ConvertAll 1.2.0
releases.body:
**Download:** `ConvertAll-1.2.0-windows.zip` below. Unzip it and run `ConvertAll\ConvertAll.exe`. Nothing to install. Keep `ConvertAll.exe` next to its `_internal` folder.

### 2026-10-30: ConvertAll 1.2.0

- **Changed: Calibre is no longer needed.** Every ebook conversion is now done by [bookport](https://github.com/puretechteam/bookport), a pure-Python ebook library made for ConvertAll (3.0 MB, against Calibre's 666.5 MB install). Measured against Calibre 9.17 on the same 13 books (median per conversion):
  - **Faster and lighter:** EPUB → PDF in 1.40 s and 40 MB of memory instead of 8.91 s and 1,138 MB. EPUB → MOBI in 0.96 s instead of 1.60 s. Python's documentation CHM → EPUB in 20.5 s instead of 381.8 s.
  - **Cleaner books:** Kindle books turned into EPUB have 0 epubcheck errors, against Calibre's 7,212.
  - **Nothing lost:** words, chapter titles, pictures, metadata and covers are kept as well as or better than Calibre does it, for every output format.
  - The Calibre engine is gone from ☰ → *Engines…* and `convertall engines`. An installed Calibre is simply no longer used.
- **Added: more ebook formats.** HTMLZ, TXTZ, FictionBook in a zip (fbz), PML and PMLZ (eReader), Rocket eBook (rb), Psion TCR and Shanda Bambook (snb), read and written. LIT, LRF and Palm (pdb) can now be written too, not only read. Ebooks also go to Word, RTF, HTML and Markdown, and every ebook format reaches every other. ConvertAll now offers 12,463 conversions (11,419 before).
- **Added: page size and text size for ebooks as PDF.** Two settings in *Options*, shown when an ebook becomes a PDF: page size (phone, 6-inch e-reader, A5, A4, Letter) and text size (small, normal, large). The command line takes `--page-size` and `--text-size`.
- **Changed: ebooks to PDF and text keep more of the book.** These used to go through PyMuPDF. On 10 books with a reference text, bookport kept a median 99.99% of the words in PDF (PyMuPDF: 98.62%), with 22% smaller files. As text, the worst book kept 99.48% of its words instead of 81.73%.
- **Added: comics become fixed-layout ebooks.** CBZ, CBR, CB7 and CBT become fixed-layout EPUB, MOBI, AZW3 and the other picture-holding formats, one page per picture, with their ComicInfo title. Pages in formats readers don't take (HEIC, TIFF, AVIF) are converted to JPG or PNG.
- **Added: ebooks are checked after converting.** ConvertAll counts the words in the original and in the result, also when the book becomes a PDF, Word, RTF, HTML, Markdown or text file; a difference of more than 3% (and more than 20 words) is reported. On 3 novels, at every page and text size and in every document format (60 conversions), the counts agreed within 4 words. Counting adds about 0.8 s to a 78,500-word novel made into a PDF.
- **Copy-protected ebooks** (DRM) are refused with a clear message. ConvertAll never removes DRM.

- **Added: ConvertAll says what a conversion can't keep.** Point at a format in the list and its tooltip gives the route (*via PDF*) and, in plain words, what that route leaves out: *"JPG has no transparency: see-through areas become white"*, *"STL holds one mesh: all parts are merged into one"*, *"CSV holds one table: only the first sheet is kept"*, *"Formulas become their last saved values"*, *"GIF animations run at 12 frames a second, at most 640 pixels wide, with 256 colors and no sound"*: 41 kinds in all, written from what each step really does. 5,926 of the 11,419 routes ConvertAll offers carry at least one. After converting, the notes are about *that* file: a PNG without transparency doesn't get the transparency note, a one-page PDF doesn't get "a folder of pages". The status line shows the first; hover it for all.
- **Added: every result is checked.** After each conversion ConvertAll opens the result the way the next program would and compares what it can measure with the original: pages, frames, picture size, transparency, length, sound tracks, parts, triangles, model size, animation, skeletons, sheets, records, subtitles, glyphs, files, places. Only measured facts are reported, never a score. A difference the route said it would make (*Parts: 4 → 1* for STL) is expected; any other, or a result that doesn't open, turns the status line amber and says what didn't match. The file is always kept. On the standard test set (192 conversions, the most common one for each format) it made 263 checks with **0 false alarms**, and on every built-in conversion of pictures, 3D models, data, tables, subtitles, fonts and maps (975) 2,100 checks, also 0 once the three real problems that sweep found were fixed (below), and the test suite now fails if a check ever disagrees unexplained. It adds 26 ms a conversion on average (35.5 → 40.5 s for all 192, same machine; files over 200 MB aren't read again).
- **Added: Details after converting.** A *Details* link next to *Show in folder* opens the report: the route and the tool that did each step (with its version), the settings used, what was left out, and a table of what was checked, before and after. *Copy report* puts it on the clipboard as JSON.
- **Changed: routes keep the most.** When there's more than one way to get there, a route now costs what it loses as well as its steps, so the one that keeps more wins even when it is a step longer. 49 of the 11,419 routes changed, every one keeping more than before: old Excel .xls/.xlsb/.xlsm and OpenDocument .ods workbooks go to JSON, YAML, XML, SQLite and the rest through XLSX (every sheet) instead of CSV (the first sheet only), SQLite databases to ODS, XLS and PDF the same way, and Visio, CorelDRAW and OpenDocument drawings to EPS through PDF (still vectors) instead of PNG. GLB ↔ glTF now goes through meshport instead of trimesh, which kept the mesh but dropped animation, skeletons and blend shapes (an animated glTF → GLB had 1 animation before and 0 after; now 1).
- **Added: files named for the wrong format are converted as what they are.** A JPEG saved as `.png` (common with downloads), a PNG named `.jpg`, a PDF, WebP, HEIC, AVIF, GIF, TIFF, BMP or Photoshop file under another of those names: ConvertAll reads the start of the file and, when it clearly says another format, uses that, and the report says *"This .png file is really a JPG"*. Converting such a file to its own real format says so instead of failing with "Can't convert JPG to JPG".
- **Added: options and presets.** A collapsed **Options** card under the format shows only the settings the chosen conversion takes: quality (JPG, WebP, AVIF, HEIC), maximum size (pictures), resolution (PDF pages to pictures or comics), video quality (smaller, balanced, best), video size (360p to 2160p, never enlarging), frame rate (video, GIF, animated WebP), sound bitrate (MP3, AAC, Ogg, Opus and the other lossy formats), and mesh detail (STEP, IGES, BREP to STL). Quality is a slider. Size, resolution, frame rate and bitrate list the usual values (1920 px, 300 dpi, 30 fps, 192 kbps...) and take any other you type. Presets are one click: *Default*, *Smaller for email and web*, *Best quality*, *For phones and social*, *Ready for 3D printing*, each shown only where it changes something. Change a setting yourself and *+ Save as preset* keeps it (in `%APPDATA%\ConvertAll\presets.json`, shared with the command line). The card's header says what's on (*Default*, the preset's name, or *Max size 1920 px*). Nothing set keeps ConvertAll's usual defaults, and each setting says what that default is, with hints only where they apply (frame rate says *Original (12 for GIF)* when making a GIF, *Original* otherwise). Measured on the test files: JPG quality 40 makes a photo under 70% of the default's size, resolution 300 draws a 4 × 2 inch page at 1200 × 600 pixels, mesh detail *fine* makes over twice the triangles of *coarse*, and sound at 256 kbps is over 2.5 times the size of 64 kbps.
- **Changed: a cleaner window.** Every screen was gone over (23 of them, in light and dark mode):
  - **Nothing overlaps.** The window's height now follows what it shows. With *Options* open, it could be made 430 px tall while its contents needed 475, so the format list slid over the drop area. Opening *Options* grows the window to fit, and closing it gives the height back.
  - **The drop area shows the file:** a small picture of a photo or of a PDF's first page, anything else as a page with its extension, several files as a stack. The file's size is shown under its name.
  - **The line under the buttons** says what happened (*Saved photo.jpg*, *Couldn't convert photo.heic*), with what the route couldn't keep, or why it failed, in grey under it. It takes no room while there's nothing to say.
  - **Dropdowns, lists, sliders and tooltips match the theme**, and every control in a row has the same height. The *Details* dialog shows each file as a card, with *Same*, *Changed*, *As noted* or *Didn't match* beside each check (and numbers like 6.633, not 6.63325). *Engines* has a *Close* button and shows which tools are installed in green. The Discord link in *About* is readable in dark mode.
- **Added: command line.** `--plan` shows each file's route, what it can't keep and the settings it takes, and converts nothing. `--json` prints one JSON object per file, and nothing else, on stdout, always as UTF-8: a report after converting (route, steps, notes, checks, warnings), the plan with `--plan` (route, steps, notes, settings, what the route takes, engines it needs), and every target with `--list` (format, kind, route, engines it needs). `--preset NAME` and the settings (`--quality`, `--max-size`, `--dpi`, `--video-quality`, `--video-size`, `--fps`, `--bitrate`, `--detail`) work as in the window; `convertall presets` lists them (*Default* included, which sets nothing). Text output prints the notes and checks under each file.
- **Added: Start menu shortcut.** ☰ → *Add to Start menu* puts ConvertAll in Start, so typing "ConvertAll" there opens it; the same item removes it.
- **Changed: the right-click menu follows the app.** Before, only a newer version repointed it, so after moving or reinstalling ConvertAll the menu kept opening the old copy. Now the installed app takes the menu over whenever the menu points at another copy of the same version, and an older copy never takes it back.
- **Changed: faster.** Measured on the same PC, before and after:
  - Right-clicking more files while ConvertAll is open hands them over in 177 ms instead of 420 ms (250 ms in the installed app, counting its own start). The handing-over process no longer loads the window or the converters.
  - The window code loads in 290 ms instead of 383 ms. The converters load just after the window shows.
  - Dropping another file takes 2.5 ms instead of 51 ms, because ConvertAll looks for newly installed engines at most every 10 seconds. Before, it searched every folder on PATH for each missing engine on every drop.
  - `convertall --plan` on 100 files takes 0.35 s instead of 1.21 s. Batches reuse the route found for the first file of each kind.
- **Fixed: piped `--json` wasn't valid UTF-8.** Output sent to a file or another program used the Windows code page, so an accented file name (`café.png`) made the JSON unreadable as UTF-8, and the route arrow came out as `?`.
- **Fixed: CSV made from JSON, YAML, XML, spreadsheets and other data showed accents wrong in Excel.** It now starts with the byte-order mark Excel looks for, as contacts already did. Both now use the same writer. TSV stays without one.
- **Fixed:** `convertall engines --install` crashed with a traceback when winget was missing or an install failed; it now says why. It also no longer accepts WinRAR, which ConvertAll never offers.
- **Fixed:** when FFmpeg was installed while ConvertAll was open, sound and video results stayed unchecked until a restart.
- **Changed:** meshport, packport and bookport are pinned to their `v0.3.0`, `v0.2.1` and `v0.1.0` tags.
- **Added: a Python API.** `from convertall import convert, plan, extract, Report`; `convert(path, "jpg", report=Report(), options={...})`.
- **Fixed: photo details and color profiles were dropped.** Converting a photo threw away its EXIF (camera, date, place) and its color profile, so wide-gamut photos (an iPhone's, for one) could shift in color and photo libraries lost their dates. They're now kept for JPG, PNG, WebP, TIFF, HEIC and AVIF (the picture is turned upright first, and its rotation flag reset).
- **Fixed: a Photoshop file with layers became an animation.** Converting a layered PSD to PNG, GIF, WebP, AVIF or TIFF made an animation of the flattened picture and some of its layers (a 2-layer test file came out as 2 frames, the second one a single layer). It's now the flattened picture alone.
- **Fixed: an OBJ's objects became one part.** Converting a multi-object OBJ to GLB, glTF, 3MF, FBX, USD, Alembic or 3DS merged its objects into one mesh (trimesh reads them as one); each object is a part of its own again (the 2-object test file: 1 part before, 2 now).
- **Fixed: a database with several tables came out as one line in JSON Lines,** holding every table; it now gets the first table, one record a line, and says so. Plist output keeps tables and keys in their order instead of sorting them.
- **Fixed: a workbook with several sheets came out as one row of JSON text in CSV/TSV.** CSV and TSV hold one table, so they now get the first sheet (or a database's first table), and the conversion says so.

- **Fixed (security): extracting archives is safer.** An audit of every way ConvertAll unpacks archives (ZIP, 7z, TAR in all its compressions, CPIO, single-file compressors, and 7-Zip for RAR, ISO, RPM and the rest) found gaps, now closed. Extracting a comic or repacking an archive goes through the same checks. New rules, the same for every extractor (`convertall/safety.py`):
  - **Nothing lands outside the folder.** Names with `..` are left out. Leading slashes and drive letters are dropped, as unzip and tar do.
  - **No links.** Symbolic links, hard links that point out, junctions and device files are left out. A sweep after every extraction removes any link that slipped through, without following it. A hard link inside a TAR becomes a copy of its file.
  - **Names Windows can't take are renamed the way 7-Zip does:** `a:b` (which would have written a hidden alternate data stream) becomes `a_b`, `CON.txt` becomes `_CON.txt`, and a trailing dot or space becomes `_`. Before, these failed or wrote somewhere unexpected.
  - **Nothing is overwritten.** Two entries with the same name, or names that differ only in case (one file on Windows), used to overwrite each other silently. The second is now saved as `name (1).ext`.
  - **Archive bombs stop.** Before anything is written, the archive's declared size is checked against the free disk space (ZIP, 7z, external 7-Zip). Single-file compressors (`.gz`, `.xz`, `.zst`…), TAR streams and CPIO are counted as they unpack. An archive that holds more data than it declares is stopped.
  - **7-Zip gets the same rules.** Before extracting, ConvertAll reads 7-Zip's listing and excludes links and escaping names. 7-Zip is also told to rename clashing names instead of overwriting them. 7-Zip releases older than 25.00 can be tricked into writing through a link (CVE-2025-11001 and 11002), so ConvertAll suggests updating. Links are excluded either way. Password prompts can no longer hang a conversion.
  - **Clear messages.** Password-protected archives say so. Damaged ones say *"looks damaged"* with the reason, instead of an "unexpected error". Disk-space refusals give the sizes. No half-extracted folder is left behind.
  - Anything left out or renamed is reported: on the status line in the window (hover for every note), and after the result in `convertall --extract`.
  - `tests/test_archive_safety.py` has 30 tests that build hostile and damaged archives in code. They cover escaping names, Windows names, duplicates, case clashes, symbolic and hard links, device files, encrypted, truncated and corrupted files, and bombs, plus the CVE pattern through 7-Zip. Every test checks that nothing outside the folder changed and no link was left.
  - One limit: 7z archives read by the built-in reader (py7zr) can't extract names containing `:`. Those entries are left out and counted.
- **Fixed (security): a downloaded file can't reach other files, the network or a planted program.** A review of every engine call and built-in reader found these, now closed. `tests/test_hardening.py` builds each hostile file in code; 16 of its tests failed before these fixes and pass now.
  - **Pandoc runs sandboxed.** An include line in a reStructuredText, LaTeX, Org or AsciiDoc file (`.. include:: C:/Users/you/notes.txt`) used to copy that file into the result. Pandoc now reads only the file it's given. Pictures still come along: ConvertAll embeds the ones in the file's own folder or one level up (never absolute, network or further-out paths), so Word, OpenDocument, EPUB and HTML results keep them as before.
  - **No programs from the current folder.** Windows looks for a program in the current folder before PATH, so a Downloads folder holding a file named `ffmpeg.exe` could have been run. Engines, winget and Explorer are now found on PATH or by full path only.
  - **FFmpeg reads local files only.** A playlist or concat file can no longer make FFmpeg (or the check after converting) fetch a URL.
  - **ImageMagick reads only the format ConvertAll planned.** The input is handed over under a plain name with its format named outright (`XCF:in.xcf`), and a policy turns off ImageMagick's script, text and URL readers. A file named for the wrong format (a PNG saved as `.jpg`) still converts.
  - **Size limits on compressed pictures and maps.** An `.svgz` or `.kmz` that unpacks to more than 512 MB is refused with a message instead of filling memory.
  - **Only you can hand files to the open window.** The local connection the right-click menu uses is now limited to your Windows account.
- **Fixed:** checking a sound or video result flashed a console window, and could misread file names with accents. FFprobe now runs hidden and in UTF-8.
- **Fixed:** right-clicking files while ConvertAll was starting or closing could open a second window. A launch now waits up to 15 seconds for the open window, then says it isn't answering instead of opening another.
- **Fixed: saved presets.** Saving or deleting a preset deleted any hand-edited preset with a value this version doesn't take; those are now kept as they are, and a `presets.json` that isn't valid JSON is set aside as `presets.unreadable.json` instead of written over. Preset names ignore case, so saving "web" replaces "Web" instead of making a second one, and "default" can't hide the built-in *Default*. The preset lit in *Options* is judged only by the settings the conversion takes, so a JPG at quality 75 and 1920 px lights *Smaller for email and web*.
- **Fixed:** a comic with both `07.jpg` and `07.webp` lost a page when it became an ebook (the converted WebP was written over the JPG). Pages left out of a comic (unsafe names) are now reported, as they are for PDF.
- **Fixed:** an ebook named for the wrong format is read as what it really is, the way the route was planned.
- **Fixed:** `--max-size 1920px` (no space) was refused; any spacing and case of the unit now works.
- **Fixed:** installing an engine from ☰ → *Engines…* now refreshes the format list at once, instead of after the next drop.
- **Fixed:** two document conversions at once in separate ConvertAll processes (the window and the command line, or a script running several) failed every other time, because both started LibreOffice on the same profile. The second now waits for the first: 0 of 28 failed with two and four at once, against 8 of 16 before.
- **Changed:** big counts in *Details* and the command line's report read 30,682 instead of 30682 (picture sizes like 1920 stay as they are).
- **Fixed: messages instead of tracebacks** for a GeoJSON file laid out in an unexpected way, a damaged archive in `--extract`, a locked file in `--plan`, `convertall view` with no ConvertAll.exe beside it, and a Start menu shortcut PowerShell couldn't write without saying why. The install question goes to stderr, so `--json` output stays JSON.
- **Changed: faster settings.** Dragging the quality slider took 3.6 ms of ConvertAll's own work a step and now takes 1.1 ms (13.8 → 11.3 ms with drawing): presets are read again only when `presets.json` changes, and the format list's notes follow once the slider rests. Checking a 12-megapixel picture for transparency takes 53 ms instead of 63 ms (38 instead of 51 for grey with transparency) and 94 MB of memory at most instead of 143 MB.
- **Changed: Blender is no longer needed.** `.blend`, USD (usd, usda, usdc, usdz) and Alembic files are now read and written by [meshport](https://github.com/puretechteam/meshport) (`.blend` is read only, as before), the same pure-Python library that took over FBX and 3DS. Blender was a 1 GB install, and the last engine any 3D format needed.
  - **Smaller:** the three formats add 266 KB to the app (388.83 → 389.10 MB unpacked, viewer included before and after). Blender was a 1 GB install.
  - **Faster:** every conversion measured got faster, by 1.8 to 5.5 times (full app runs on one PC, best of 3): a 3-object .blend → GLB 2.13 → 0.43 s, a 660,000-triangle .blend → GLB 2.41 → 0.93 s, USDZ → 3MF 3.33 → 1.31 s, Alembic → STL 2.01 → 1.13 s, GLB → USDZ 2.31 → 0.44 s, GLB → Alembic 2.23 → 0.40 s.
  - **Same results:** meshport reads Blender's own USD, Alembic and .blend files to the same geometry as Blender's conversion did (19 of 19 files), reads 13 tricky USD files the same way Pixar's own USD library does, and the USD files it writes pass all of Pixar's validators. The files it writes are no bigger than Blender's: USDZ 672 KB vs 759 KB, Alembic 909 KB vs 1.03 MB.
  - **.blend files now come out as Blender shows them:** the modifiers that are on in Blender's viewport are applied (Triangulate, Weld, Mirror, Array, Solidify and Subdivision Surface; others are skipped), and curve, text and metaball objects become meshes. The old conversion through Blender didn't apply modifiers. Text in Blender's built-in font uses a similar installed font, so its letters come out a few percent wider or narrower.
  - **Older .blend files checked:** files saved by Blender 2.83, 2.93, 3.3 and 3.5 come out the same as each of those versions converts them. This check found that every mesh with a UV map from Blender 2.8 to 3.4 was refused as damaged; that is fixed.
  - **Still to come:** other modifiers (Bevel, Boolean, Geometry Nodes, ...), bevel and taper objects on curves, and NURBS surfaces.
  - The Blender engine is gone from ☰ → *Engines…* and `convertall engines`. An installed Blender is simply no longer used.
- **Added: animation survives conversion.** Converting between FBX, GLB/glTF, USD (usd, usda, usdc, usdz) and Alembic now keeps the objects' movement (position, rotation and scale), and animated 3DS and Blender files bring theirs along too (to any of those). Before, the result was a still model. FBX and glTF keep every animation take; USD and Alembic have one timeline, so they keep the first. Formats without animation (OBJ, STL, 3MF, ...) keep the first frame.
- **Added: animated models play in the viewer.** Open an animated model in the big viewer (FBX, glTF, USD, Alembic, 3DS or Blender) and it plays: moving parts, rigged characters bending, blend shapes changing. Play or pause it (the button or the space bar), drag along the timeline to any moment, and pick which take to play when the file has several (takes that move different things, as Blender exports each object's action, play together by default). The view frames the model and sets its ground grid for the whole animation, not just its first frame. The preview in the drop area plays it too (and says it's animated under it), pausing while the big viewer has it open. A model too heavy to pose 60 times a second plays fewer frames a second instead of slowing ConvertAll down, and a preview nobody can see costs nothing. Shading follows blend shapes as they change.
- **Added: rigged characters and face shapes survive conversion.** A character's skeleton and how its mesh bends with it (skinning), and its blend shapes (shape keys, morph targets) with their animated weights, now come across between FBX, GLB/glTF and USD, and from Blender files. Before, a rigged character came out stiff in its rest pose. Checked against Blender and Pixar's own USD library: they bend ConvertAll's files exactly as ConvertAll bends theirs.
