Formats without skeletons (3DS, OBJ, STL, 3MF, PLY, ...) get the mesh where its skeleton holds it, its shapes applied, and Alembic gets its motion as a point cache. Checked with Khronos' rigged sample characters too (CesiumMan, BrainStem, Fox and others): Blender, Pixar's USD library and Autodesk's FBX library all bend ConvertAll's FBX and USD of them as ConvertAll does. Blend shapes with in-between shapes (FBX, USD) and Blender's bone options (inherit rotation, inherit scale) come across as well.
- **Fixed: some FBX models came out turned wrongly.** An FBX model's pre- and post-rotation only count when the file turns them on (most exporters that use them do). ConvertAll used to apply them always; now it follows Autodesk's own FBX library, as Blender does.
- **Added: a 3D viewer.** Drop one 3D model or CAD part on the window and it shows in the drop area, live: drag to turn it, right-drag to move it, scroll to zoom toward the cursor, arrow keys and +/- work too. The expand button in its corner, or a double-click, opens a big viewer window with a wireframe view and a summary (parts, triangles, materials, and the size in meters, or in the file's own units for STL, OBJ, 3MF and CAD files).
  - It opens everything ConvertAll can turn into a 3D model: glb gltf fbx 3ds usd usdz abc blend stl obj ply off 3mf dae, and CAD parts (step iges brep). Textures, vertex colors, see-through materials and mirrored parts show as they should. Models without normals get smooth shading on curved surfaces and crisp edges where faces meet at over 40°.
  - **View with ConvertAll** in Explorer's right-click menu (on 3D models and CAD parts) opens just the viewer, and `convertall view model.fbx` does the same from a terminal.
  - It draws with Qt's own GPU layer (Direct3D 11 on Windows), so it needs no extra libraries: the built app grew by 74 KB (388.76 → 388.83 MB unpacked).
- **Added: a Discord for help and chat** ([invite](https://discord.gg/dRMRGCG9Fk)), in the window's menu (☰ → *Help and chat on Discord*), the About box and the README.
- **Changed:** the menu button is now a clear ☰ that lights up on hover and while its menu is open, instead of three faint dots; the viewer's expand button is drawn the same way. Both follow light and dark mode and look the same on every PC (the old ones were font characters, which Windows showed as a small colored emoji).
- **Fixed:** previewing a CAD part while converting another one could run gmsh on two threads at once; they now take turns.
- **Changed:** ConvertAll needs PySide6 6.7 or newer (for `QRhiWidget`).

releases.name: ConvertAll 1.1.0
releases.body:
**Download:** `ConvertAll-1.1.0-windows.zip` below. Unzip it and run `ConvertAll\ConvertAll.exe`. Nothing to install. Keep `ConvertAll.exe` next to its `_internal` folder.

### 2026-10-26: Safer 3D files, old Windows text files, and the app moves to Releases (part of 1.1.0)

- **Fixed (security):** a 3D model's texture paths could name any file on the computer, and converting the model to FBX, 3DS or OBJ copied that file into the output. ConvertAll now uses [meshport 0.2.0](https://github.com/puretechteam/meshport/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md), which only takes files that are really images and never opens network paths.
- **Fixed:** subtitles, web pages, HTML → PDF, CSV, JSON, YAML, TOML, XML and INI files saved in older Windows encodings (Windows-1252) or as "Unicode" (UTF-16) keep their accented letters. Before, accents turned into "�" in some conversions and CSV files from Excel failed outright. One shared reader (`convertall/textfile.py`) replaces three copies of the same fallback.
- **Fixed:** an unexpected error during a conversion or engine install could leave the window's progress bar spinning forever. It now shows the error.
- **Changed:** when Explorer hands files to an already open window, the sending process now waits until the whole list is written, and the window waits until the sender is done, instead of both assuming the list goes across in one piece. A test sends 5,000 file names (665 KB) between two processes.
- **Changed:** CPIO archives are extracted by [packport 0.2.0](https://github.com/puretechteam/packport/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md), which streams them to disk instead of loading them into memory.
- **Changed:** the ready-to-run app is no longer kept in the repository's `app` folder (369 MB per build, in every clone). Download it as a zip from [Releases](https://github.com/puretechteam/ConvertAll/releases/latest); `packaging/release.py` builds the zip.
- **Changed:** meshport and packport are pinned to their `v0.2.0` tags, and the libraries ConvertAll imports directly (Beautiful Soup, NumPy, backports.zstd before Python 3.14) are listed as dependencies instead of arriving by chance through other packages.
- **Changed:** the window starts a little faster: the download code for Ghostscript loads only when Ghostscript is being installed. Ghostscript downloads are also only accepted from Artifex's own GitHub releases.
- **Added:** GitHub Actions run the tests and `ruff check` on every push and pull request, plus `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `SECURITY.md`. The code passes ruff 0.16's default rules.

### 2026-10-26: Extract from the right-click menu, every archive type, and 62 more formats (1.1.0)

ConvertAll now reads 245 formats (was 183) and writes 150 (was 116).

- **Added: "Extract with ConvertAll"** in Explorer's right-click menu on archives. It unpacks straight away, with progress, then "Saved …" and *Show in folder*. Select several archives and they're extracted as one batch. Other files and folders still get "Convert with ConvertAll". An existing right-click menu updates itself the first time the new version opens.
- **Added: RAR and CBR output**, written by [packport](https://github.com/puretechteam/packport), a new pure-Python library (the way meshport replaced Blender for FBX). They're RAR 4 *stored* archives, which every reader opens, including old comic apps. If WinRAR is installed, ConvertAll uses it instead for real compression. packport also writes Unix `.Z` and CPIO.
- **Added: every common archive and compression type.**
  - New outputs: rar, tar.lz4, lz4, br (Brotli), lzma, z, cpio, iso (with Joliet and Rock Ridge, so long and non-English names survive) and wim.
  - New inputs: disk images (vmdk, vdi, qcow2, img, squashfs, udf, apfs, hfs), macOS installers (xar, pkg), Windows patches (msp), Unix ar, zipx, and split archives (.001, .r00).
  - Zip-based packages each show under their own name and extract like a zip: jar, war, ear, apk, aab, ipa, xpi, crx, vsix, nupkg, whl, appx and msix.
- **Added: new formats.**
  - **Images:** any picture → **SVG**, traced into real vector shapes; PSD, CUR, XPM and EPS outputs; EPS and PostScript inputs; gzipped SVG (.svgz).
  - **Audio and video:** M4R iPhone ringtones; DSD audio (dsf, dff) and 3G2 inputs.
  - **Subtitles:** YouTube SBV, MicroDVD SUB, TTML/DFXP and SAMI. ASS/SSA no longer need FFmpeg.
  - **Documents:**
    - LaTeX, reStructuredText, Org, AsciiDoc and MediaWiki ↔ Markdown, HTML, Word, OpenDocument and EPUB, through Pandoc;
    - DjVu → PDF and text, through DjVuLibre;
    - Hangul (HWP) and dBASE (DBF) inputs;
    - Jupyter notebooks → Markdown/HTML, including saved outputs and plots;
    - saved web pages (MHT/MHTML) → HTML/PDF with their pictures inlined;
    - CHM help files → EPUB/PDF/MOBI.
  - **New kind, Email:** EML and Outlook MSG → PDF, HTML or text, with headers, inline pictures and the list of attachments.
  - **New kind, Maps:** GPX, KML, KMZ and GeoJSON to each other, and → CSV.
  - **Contacts and calendars:** vCard and iCalendar ↔ CSV/JSON (and on to Excel). Google and Outlook CSV exports are understood.
  - **Fonts:** TTF ↔ OTF (TrueType and CFF outlines converted), and TTC collections split into their fonts.
  - **3D:** 3DS read and write, through meshport 0.2.
  - **CAD:** SVG and PDF vector drawings → DXF, for laser cutters.
  - **Data:** SQLite as an output.
- **Added: three engines, each installed from the window like the others:**
  - **Pandoc** and **DjVuLibre**, both through winget;

## FrameKeep 3.1.1: Recordings fix

A quick fix for 3.1.0. If you're on 3.1.0, please update.

### Fixed
- **Opening Recordings closed FrameKeep** with "Unhandled exception in script". The page now opens normally, and new tests open it and resize it the way the app does.
- **Recordings now stop when FrameKeep stops.** If FrameKeep closed unexpectedly, 3.1.0 left its screen recorder running in the background, one more after every restart, and Windows showed "Failed to remove temporary directory". Now Windows ends them together with FrameKeep: in testing, a recorder was gone 157 ms after FrameKeep was force-closed (before: still running). Files are saved every 5 seconds, so a crash costs at most the last few seconds.
- **The Recordings grid follows the window size** again, adding or removing columns as you resize.

### Changed
- The player uses [puretech-player 0.1.1](https://github.com/puretechteam/puretech-player), which keeps its clock on the frame you stepped to.

**If 3.1.0 crashed on you:** a recorder may still be running in the background. Restarting your PC stops it, or end any `ffmpeg.exe` in Task Manager. Your recordings are not affected.

### Download
Get **FrameKeep.exe** below. It's one portable file with everything inside: no Python, no installer. Your settings carry over.

Full notes: [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/puretechteam/framekeep/blob/v3.1.1/CHANGELOG.md) · **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/puretechteam/framekeep/compare/v3.1.0...v3.1.1

releases.name: FrameKeep 3.1.0
releases.body:
## FrameKeep 3.1: your screen and your cameras, in tiny files

The biggest FrameKeep update yet. FrameKeep now records your **webcams and network cameras** next to your screen, has its **own player**, can record **desktop audio**, and the app itself got much lighter. Every number below was measured, and the full tables are in [docs/perf](https://github.com/puretechteam/framekeep/blob/v3.1.0/docs/perf/README.md).

![The FrameKeep player: desktop and two cameras side by side](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/puretechteam/framekeep/v3.1.0/docs/screenshots/player.png)

### Cameras
Turn webcams, capture cards, phones (Iriun, DroidCam) and network cameras (RTSP or HTTP) into a recording station inside FrameKeep.
- Records around the clock with no gap between files, and marks **motion on a timeline** you can jump straight to.
- Optional per camera: sound, date and time in the picture, motion notifications, "save space when nothing moves".
- Runs separately from screen recording. Pause your own webcam for a call from the tray, a hotkey, or automatically while apps like Zoom are open.
- **86 MB per hour** for a 720p webcam in AV1 (still scene), 2 to 3% of the PC's CPU. At the same quality AV1 was 2.8x smaller than H.265 and 10x smaller than H.264.
- Network cameras can keep their own stream for almost no CPU (0.05%), or be made smaller.

![Cameras page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/puretechteam/framekeep/v3.1.0/docs/screenshots/cameras.png)

### The FrameKeep player
**Play** now opens FrameKeep's own player instead of ffplay.
- A whole day plays as **one timeline** across files, in every format FrameKeep records, H.266 included.
- Up to **four sources side by side** (desktop and cameras) in sync, with saved layouts and the sound from the one you pick.
- Time bar with a lane per source and motion marks, 0.25x to 16x, frame stepping, next/previous motion.
- **Lossless clip export**: set In and Out and save a full-quality copy in a moment.
- Against ffplay on 8 test files: less or equal CPU on all 8 (H.266 at 1080p: 52% of a core instead of 108%), less memory on 7, faster seeks on 6. Built on [puretech-player](https://github.com/puretechteam/puretech-player).

### Desktop audio (optional, off by default)
- Records what your PC plays into the same file: Opus (smallest) or AAC (plays everywhere). Silence costs about 1 kbps.
- Follows headphone and speaker switches, and can leave apps out (for example Discord).
- Adds about 21 MB of memory and 0.1% of the PC's CPU.

### Lighter and smarter
- A **native tray** ([puretech-tray](https://github.com/puretechteam/puretech-tray)): the icon shows motion and problems, notifications have buttons (**Play** on a motion alert), and the menu follows dark mode. FrameKeep uses 16% less memory in the tray with it.
- Compared with 3.0: the app commits **21 MB instead of 520 MB** in the tray, wakes up 3 times a second instead of 90, and encoders use up to 24% less memory.
- **Disk space**: a warning once recordings pass 100 GB (you choose), and optional cleanup of old camera footage. Desktop recordings are never deleted.
- H.266 (Ultra) recordings now play back with correct timing.

### Download
Get **FrameKeep.exe** below. It's one portable file with everything inside, FFmpeg included: no Python, no installer.

**Upgrading from 3.0:** your settings carry over. The Player setting becomes "FrameKeep player". The first time FrameKeep shows a notification it adds a Start menu shortcut for your account, because Windows only shows notifications with buttons for apps that have one.

**Good to know:** H.265 on cameras can fall behind on busy scenes, so cameras default to AV1. On a 2-core PC, three cameras watching constant movement fall behind; use fewer or a lower frame rate.

Full notes: [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/puretechteam/framekeep/blob/v3.1.0/CHANGELOG.md) · [README](https://github.com/puretechteam/framekeep/blob/v3.1.0/README.md) · **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/puretechteam/framekeep/compare/v3.0.0...v3.1.0

Licensed under GPLv3 - see LICENSE file for details

v2.0.0 Changelog
- Fixed FrameKeep not being able to sometimes find openh264-1.8.0-win64.dll on startup
- Added ffmpeg.exe to handle automatic but safe .mkv → .mp4 conversions (you can download your own ffmpeg build, using a different build could cause script instability), this does add ~100MB to the final build. You can delete the .exe and/or turn this off in the configuration file if you wish.
- Added CRF (Constant Rate Factor) so .mkv → .mp4 conversions are not only safe, but will also save storage space. You can turn CRF off in the configuration .json file, you can also edit the CRF value in the config file, the default is 23 to maintain quality while getting smaller files. CRF is automatically ignored if .mkv → .mp4 conversions are turned off.
- Added the "chunk_minutes" option to the configuration file, this allows you to change how long you want each file to record for. The default has been left at 60 minutes
- Important actions added to the console. Also added color coding, and timestamps.
- Added folders for third-party software to clean the repo up.
- Fixed build version to match Semantic Versioning standards (hopefully), also started saving releases for older versions. FrameKeepOS, FFmpeg, and Cisco's Open H.264 licensing has been added to the repo.
- Adjusted H.264 ADUS to new averages done with personal testing (users are more than welcome to post their own results, they will be taken into account with ADUS numbers).

Future Plans
- FrameKeep only records the primary monitor, I hope to add configuration settings that let you choose all, or certain monitors.
- Plan on implementing a "frame-break" system that automatically detects when the same frame is being displayed (for say, 5 or 10 frames), and saves space by not saving that frame repeatedly. While CRF and H.264 are good at this on their own, a correct system could save even more storage space.
- H.265 and AV1 are in the plans, and will NOT be replacing the defaults, they will be optional bonuses to users that can computationally afford it.

childlock.description: Lock your keyboard and mouse with one shortcut so kids can mash keys without anything happening. Type a secret word to unlock. Windows 10/11.

releases.name: ChildLock v0.2.0
releases.body:
New:

- Lock only the keyboard or only the mouse, from the tray (**Lock only**) or as the default for the hotkey and auto-lock. A mouse-only lock ends when you press the hotkey again.
- Hold the lock hotkey for 3 seconds (2 to 10, or off) to unlock without typing. A hotkey still held from locking never counts, and any other key starts the hold over.
- Cleaning mode: every screen goes black with a note that fades away, the keyboard and mouse are locked, and it ends by itself after 60 seconds (0 to 600, or never) by fading the screens back in.
- The badge shows on every monitor and follows monitor changes. It can be hidden (the countdown always shows), and can show a dot for each correct character of the unlock word.
- The unlock word can be a phrase: any length up to 64, letters, digits and spaces. Settings warns about short, common or sequential words instead of refusing them.
- Optional: ask for the unlock word before Settings, pausing the hotkey or exiting.
- Optional: hide the unlock word from the tray tooltip.
- The tray icon, menu and notifications now use PureTech.Tray: native menus that follow Windows dark mode, toasts with buttons such as **Open Settings**, and an icon that comes back after Explorer restarts or starts late at sign-in. ChildLock adds a Start menu shortcut so its toasts show under its own name.
- Declining the admin prompt no longer stops ChildLock: it runs without admin rights, stops asking, and explains what that means. **Run as administrator** in Settings turns it back on and restarts ChildLock elevated.
- Start at sign-in works without admin rights too (per-user startup entry), and switches to the elevated task once ChildLock runs as admin.
- `--uninstall` removes the sign-in entry, the Start menu shortcut and toast registration, and optionally your settings. `--no-elevate` skips the admin prompt once.
- Settings are grouped into Locking, Unlocking, Badge and sound, Cleaning mode and Startup.
- GitHub Actions builds and unit-tests every push on Windows, and publishes `ChildLock.exe` to a release for each version tag.

Fixed:

- Keys still held down when ChildLock unlocks (the last letter of the word, or the hotkey) no longer auto-repeat into the app that has focus.
- Auto-repeat of a key held down when the lock started (such as the `L` of Ctrl+Alt+L with no countdown) no longer counts as typing the unlock word.
- Exiting during a countdown no longer runs leftover work against the closed badge and tray icon.
- The badge moves to the right place after a resolution or monitor change.
- Starting a lock closes an open Settings window instead of leaving it clickable during a keyboard-only lock.
- A failed input hook is reported as such in the diagnostics log instead of as an exit.
- Small resource leaks in the badge and the Settings window, and the diagnostics log can no longer throw when its file is locked.

bible-widget.description: A Bible verse widget for the Windows desktop: 34 free translations in 27 languages, with Find, Favorites, Save as Image and in-app updates. No install needed.

releases.name: Bible Widget 2.1.0
releases.body:
### A correction and an apology
Versions 1.1.0 through 2.0.2 included Bible translations we did not have the right to share, and our license said every Bible text was public domain. That was wrong. Four of them are copyrighted, and their publishers do not allow copying: the Nova Versão Internacional, the Almeida Corrigida Fiel, the New Chinese Version and the Finnish Kirkkoraamattu of 1992 (shipped as Pyhä Raamattu). Six more are claimed by their publishers or still protected in some countries: the Almeida Revisada Imprensa Bíblica, La Bible de l'Épée, Schlachter 1951, the Korean Revised Version of 1961, the Chinese Union Version in its 1988 New Punctuation edition and Cornilescu 1924.

We are sorry: to the translators and publishers of those Bibles, and to everyone who downloaded them trusting that they were free to share. We should have checked each text's history before shipping it, and we did not.

What we have done about it:
- All ten are removed from the app, and the releases that contained them are taken down.
- Every Bible the app ships was checked against its own history (its publisher, its translators and the dates), not only against the site it came from.
- Each one now has its license, year and source recorded in `bibles/index.json` and listed in LICENSE.
- The build and the tests refuse any Bible without that record, or with a license other than public domain or CC BY-SA 4.0.

### Added
- **34 Bible translations in 27 languages** (was 25 in 14). New languages: Czech (Kralická 1613), Danish (1871/1907), Dutch (Statenvertaling, 1917 printing), Hebrew (with the Delitzsch New Testament), Hindi and Tamil (Indian Revised Version), Hungarian (Károli 1908), Italian (Riveduta 1927), Japanese (Bungo-yaku), Latin (Clementine Vulgate), Persian (Old Persian Version), Polish (Biblia Gdańska 1881), Swahili (Unlocked Literal Bible), Swedish (1917), Tagalog (Ang Biblia 1905) and Ukrainian (Kulish 1905). Also new: Lutherbibel 1912, Louis Segond 1910 and Almeida 1911. All 6 prayers are in every translation (Job's Prayer used to be missing from one), and references work in each language, such as "Giovanni 3:16", "יוחנן 3:16" or "ヨハネ 3:16". On the real screen, 0 of 2,200 random passages from the new and re-sourced Bibles were cut off.
- **Menu in 29 languages** (was 14): Czech, Danish, Dutch, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Italian, Japanese, Persian, Polish, Swahili, Swedish, Tagalog, Tamil and Ukrainian are new. Arabic, Hebrew and Persian menus and windows now read from right to left; the widget and saved images look exactly the same either way (0 pixels differ). Where human-made wording exists, it is used: language names come from the Unicode CLDR project (870 of them, written and reviewed by native speakers), and OK, Cancel, Apply, Close and Reset to Defaults use Qt's own translations in the 20 menu languages Qt covers. Bible book names in the menus come from the book name lists of that language's Bibles. The rest of the menu text in languages other than English is machine translated; the Menu Language menu says so, with a link to suggest a better wording.
- **No install needed**: download `BibleWidget-<version>-win64.zip`, unzip, run `BibleWidget.exe`. No Python, no PySide6, no `dependencies.bat`. The download is 67 MB, with all 34 Bibles (unused Qt and Python parts are left out, which saved 24 MB). The build behaves the same as running from source: the same self-test checks pass on both, and a fresh unzip passes with Python removed from the PATH. It opens in about half a second, a little faster than v2.0.2 from source in the same test (0.50 s against 0.53 s), and uses the same memory (76 MB).
- **Updates from inside the app**: the app checks GitHub shortly after it starts and then once a day (or when you choose Check for Updates) and offers new versions with their release notes. Update Now downloads the new version, verifies its SHA-256 checksum, and lets the new version install itself, so each release brings its own installer. Checking and unpacking the download happen in the background, so the window keeps responding. The swap and restart take 2 to 3 seconds. Your settings, favorites, history and any Bibles you added are never touched, and the names you gave added Bibles in `bibles/index.json` are kept. If anything goes wrong (a file in use, or a new version that fails to start), every file is put back and the version you had starts again. If the running version hangs instead of closing for the update, it is ended after a minute so the update can go on. A window left open while the update installs (Stats, a confirmation, the color picker) is closed so the app can hand over at once, instead of holding it up until the installer ends the app. Files held for a moment by antivirus or OneDrive are retried while installing and while putting files back, and if the old version could ever not be fully put back, its files are kept in `.update-backup` instead of starting a broken app. A shipped file or folder marked read-only, hidden or system (by you or a sync tool) is updated too, and a file another program holds open the whole time is left as it was while the update is undone, with the old version started again. Tested end to end against real builds: 12 of 12 scenarios pass (successful update, bad checksum refused, failed start rolled back, installer that cannot start, offline, Skip This Version, read-only folder, short temp paths with an install folder whose name has brackets and an apostrophe, a locked file midway, a file held for 2 seconds, which is retried and then installs, files you added or edited, and an old version that hangs instead of closing). Automatic checks can be turned off in About Bible Widget. Updates replace the Bible and prayer files that ship with the app and remove the ones a new version no longer includes; if you edited one, your version is kept next to it as `<name>.edited-<date>`, and a file you added is never replaced, even by a new file with the same name.
- **Crash logging**: if the widget ever ends without being closed, the next start says so in `widget.log`, with when the run started and was last seen running (recorded every 10 minutes), its memory and handles at that time, the Python stack of every thread at the moment of a crash, and Windows' own crash or hang report for it, found by its process number. Errors in background threads and during clean-up are logged too, and so are Windows ending the app (shutting down, signing out, or closing the console it was started from) and a start with Windows' crash reports turned off. Before, a crash left nothing: no log line, and a `widget.pid` that only gave a process number. Tested by ending the real app 7 ways (Exit, ended from outside, an error in another thread, an access violation, Qt's fatal error, Ctrl+Break in its console, and an old `widget.pid`): 24 of 24 checks pass, against 8 of 24 before.
- **About Bible Widget**: shows the version number, which also appears in the tray tooltip, Stats and the exe's file properties.
- **Find a verse**: type a reference such as "John 3:16", "Jn 3:16-18", "1 Cor 13", "Jude 3", or a book name in any of the Bibles' languages ("Juan 3:16", "Giovanni 3:16", "Иоанна 3:16", "Мф 5:3"), and the whole chapter is listed with your verses highlighted and shown on the widget (Proverbs 30:4 lists all 33 verses of Proverbs 30). Numbered books can be typed with a number however the Bible writes them: "1 Jana" finds the Polish "I Jana", and the same works in Greek, Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Vietnamese and Japanese. A range that runs into the next chapter ("John 3:16-4:2") shows the first chapter's part. A word on its own, with no chapter, counts as a book name only in the translation's language or in English, so "Judas" or "esta" search the text instead of opening a book. So does a book name that is mostly another word in its own Bible: the Hebrew "יהודה" is Judah in 612 verses as well as the name of Jude, so on its own it is searched for ("יהודה 1" opens Jude), and the same goes for 26 such names in 14 languages. Numbers typed with a Japanese or Chinese keyboard (ヨハネ３：１６) work too. Names are found with or without the words in front of them ("К Римлянам", "Послание к Римлянам", "До Римлян", "Księga Rodzaju", "Waraka wa Yakobo"), in older forms ("Første Kongebog", and the Bungo-yaku's own "コリント前書", "ヨハネ傳福音書" and "列王紀略上"), and with any accent on the Greek numeral sign ("Α΄ Ιωάννου"). English short forms open the English book in every Bible: "Dan 7:13" opened Numbers in 10 of them (through the Vietnamese "Dân Số Ký"), and "Ro 1:1" opened Genesis. In a one-chapter book, "Jude 1-3" shows verses 1 to 3 (it showed 1 to 5). Or search by words across the whole Bible, with the matching words shown in bold: about 11 ms per search, and 0.15 s for the first search in a translation (0.4 s in Hindi). Words are found as keyboards type them: Vietnamese without accents ("Duc Chua Troi" finds all 3,647 verses with "Đức Chúa Trời", not 9), modern kanji in the Japanese Bible, printed in the old forms ("天国" finds the 33 verses with "天國", not 0), Persian without the zero-width non-joiner (544 verses, not 0), Hindi with or without the zero-width joiner, any kind of apostrophe ("l'Éternel" finds the 5,544 verses with "l’Éternel", not 0, and "dell'Eterno" 1,513), and the Arabic and Persian keyboards' different yeh and kaf. Searches match the start of words, in Hindi and Tamil too, where the marks that spell a word count ("परम" does not find "प्रेम") while accents elsewhere are ignored, and Japanese ガ and カ count as different letters. Arabic results line up from the right, so each verse's start is visible. Show any result on the widget, add it to your favorites, copy it or save it as an image.
- **Favorites and History**: save verses you love and look back at the last 100 verses the widget showed, in the new Verses window. Every list can show, copy or save the selected verse as an image, from its buttons or a right-click menu, and has keys: Enter shows the verse, Ctrl+C copies it, Delete removes a favorite, Ctrl+F jumps to Find and Esc closes the window. Clear History asks before it removes anything. If the favorites or history file is ever damaged, it is kept as `favorites.json.damaged-<date>` instead of being overwritten.
- **Back**: bring back the verse that just changed.
- **Save as Image**: turns a verse into a 3200x1800 card image in your colors, saved to `Pictures\Bible Widget` and copied to the clipboard. No two images are ever alike: each one paints a new background in one of 7 styles (starry night, aurora, sunrise, ocean, heavenly light, nebula, bokeh) from its own 256-bit random seed (a repeat is about 1 in 4×10³⁸ even if all 8 billion people saved one image every second for 100 years), with no watermark, just the translation name. In testing, 70 of 70 images were all different. The text is checked against the actual background behind it: the verse reaches at least 4.5:1 contrast and the reference and translation name at least 3:1 (the WCAG AA levels for normal and large text), tested on 140 cards. Readable custom colors are kept; colors that would be hard to read on a given background get another background, or the default colors. On a bright sky the translation name gets a soft dark backing. Click the notification to open the image. If the Pictures folder cannot be written, the image is still copied to the clipboard. The file is written in the background, so the widget no longer freezes while it saves: writing the PNG takes about 0.2 s, and the widget kept responding throughout (its longest pause during the write was under 1 ms). Quitting while an image is being written waits for the file to finish.
- **Right-click menu on the widget**: Back, Next Verse, Add to Favorites, Copy Verse, Save as Image, Find a Verse, Favorites & History. It opened and ran the chosen action 8 times out of 8 in real-click tests.

### Changed
- **Bibles taken out**: the ten translations above are replaced where a free one exists: Almeida 1911 for the three Portuguese ones, Lutherbibel 1912 for Schlachter, Louis Segond 1910 for La Bible de l'Épée and the Finnish Bible of 1776 for Pyhä Raamattu. We have not yet found a Chinese, Korean or Romanian text whose free status we could confirm, so the others have no replacement yet (a Korean text labeled "1910" turned out to be the 1961 Korean Revised Version, so it is not included). If you had chosen one of them, the widget and Find switch to its replacement (or the default) by themselves; favorites and history you saved from them keep their verses.
- **License**: LICENSE lists every Bible with its status and source: 30 are public domain and 4 (Hindi, Tamil, Swahili and the Wycliffe transcription) are under CC BY-SA 4.0. It also covers the language names (Unicode License) and the software the download is built with: Python (PSF License) and Qt with PySide6 (LGPL v3), with the third-party code inside Qt; their license texts come in the download's `licenses` folder.
- **Sharper tray icon**: the white cross is drawn for each display scale instead of being stretched, so at 200% scaling it has 16 soft edge pixels instead of 104, and it adds a faint warm glow. It stays white whatever Verse Text color you pick, and gets a dark edge on light taskbars, where the old icon was nearly invisible (it switches as soon as you change the Windows theme, or only the taskbar's). Windows such as Stats and Verses now show the cross as their icon.
- **Startup launcher**: two copies of the app (for example the exe and a source folder) no longer take over each other's Run on Startup entry, and Run on Startup shows as on only when it starts this copy. Choosing Off then leaves the other copy's entry alone.
- **Moving from 2.0.2**: while 2.0.2 is still running, starting the new version brings 2.0.2 forward instead of opening a second widget. The README says which five settings files to copy into the new folder to keep your settings.
- **Copy Verse** adds the translation after the reference, for example "John 11:35 (KJV)", and a notification confirms the copy.
- **A folder that can't be written**: if the app sits in a folder it can't write to (such as Program Files), a notification now says your settings can't be saved there; clicking it opens the folder. Before, settings were silently lost at every restart.
- **Running from source**: packages are listed in `requirements.txt`, which `dependencies.bat` now installs. The tests are included: `python tests/run_tests.py` runs 772 checks in about two minutes without touching your settings.
- **Less memory, same speed**: the verse of the day needs 0.5 MB of memory per Bible instead of 2.3 MB, with the same verse each day. Bibles load as fast as in 2.0.2 (the 13 that are unchanged: 325 ms together, against 328 ms) even though each verse's text is now cleaned up as it loads (see Fixed).
- **Wycliffe Bible**: now the transcription from Wikisource (through CrossWire), shared under CC BY-SA 4.0 as its license asks.
- **README screenshots** show the new menus with all 34 translations and 29 languages, the right-click menu, the Verses window and the current Customize Colors window. They come in the download too, so its README shows them.

### Fixed
- **Leftovers from the source files in the verse text**: 40,605 of the 403,387 verses in the 13 Bibles kept from 2.0.2 showed things that were never meant to be read: square brackets ("darkness [was] upon" in Webster), italics codes ("darkness <FI>is<Fi> on" in Young's Literal), backquotes, other numberings' verse numbers ("(H13:1)" in the Finnish Bible, "(14:55)" and "(75-)" in the Synodal), footnotes ("(a) Spelta eli Turkin kaura."), HTML codes ("<<" around the Greek psalm titles), invisible direction marks in the Arabic, missing spaces ("YetGod" in the ASV, "diris:Jen" in the Esperanto), margin notes in the KJV ("make...; or, fulfil"), 44 Vietnamese letters garbled into "@" or "»" ("Tr»i" for "Trời"), stars marking a gap in the Arabic and the Bible in Basic English (now an ellipsis) and a few typos ("Ela0d", ",,"). Darby, which had 3,681 missing spaces ("In the beginningGod"), now comes from eBible.org's edition. Two verse endings in the Arabic Bible (1 Timothy 6:21 and 3 John 1:14) had stray brackets and a reference in them; they now read as in the printed Van Dyck Bible. A scan of all 1,057,582 verses now finds 0 leftovers.
- **The King James Version was missing 6 verses** (Herod's order in Matthew 2:16 among them) and had split 4 others in two, so 146 verses showed under the wrong number: Find "Matthew 22:37" showed verse 38. It now has all 31,102 verses, numbered as printed, and every chapter has as many verses as Webster's revision of it.
- **Long verses cut off on small screens**: on a 1366 x 768 laptop at 125% scaling, 109 of the KJV's verses lost their ending (Esther 8:9 by 265 pixels). The widget now grows wider as well as taller for such a verse: 0 of 31,102 are cut off on that screen, or at 1280 x 720. It is also sized for the screen it is on: moved to another monitor, or after a change of resolution or scaling, it kept the size of the first screen (on a laptop, 40% of its width instead of 20%).
- **Verses that are only punctuation** ("..." in 19 verses of the Bible in Basic English, where the source lost the words or joined them to the verse before) no longer show as a passage. Find opens the next verse instead and highlights that one in the chapter list (before, nothing in the list was highlighted). The 11 such verses in the Hebrew New Testament ("׃") and the Arabic 3 John 1:1 (":") now have their words.
- **Verses lost, merged or empty in 13 Bibles**: where a source file fitted an edition's verses into another numbering, the extra verses were glued onto the verse before (Job 39:30 held nine verses in the Geneva, Danish, Polish and Swedish Bibles), and elsewhere verses were lost or left empty. They were repaired from other public domain copies of the same editions (listed in LICENSE): 459 verses are back under their own number (107 Danish, 100 Polish, 98 Swedish, 45 Hungarian, 41 Vietnamese, 29 Geneva, 26 Wycliffe, 8 Finnish, 5 Czech, Persian and Japanese), and 187 Vietnamese verses that had lost words in the middle are whole again. Checked chapter by chapter: no letter of the text was lost, the repairs only moved verse breaks or put back missing words. The Vietnamese and Finnish Bibles now have all 31,102 verses.
- **Words run together in the American Standard Version**: 644 verses had words joined where the source dropped its italics ("Godisfor us, whoisagainst us" in Romans 8:31, "Davidmade"). They are now spaced as printed, which also makes this Bible's clean-up 59% faster (142 ms to 58 ms for the whole Bible, the same for the Geneva Bible).
- **Translator's notes in the King James Version**: Luke 17:36 ended with "this verse is not found in most of the Greek copies", and Luke 10:22 with a note on other copies. Both are gone.
- **Typing errors from the source files**: a number inside a German verse ("gerechtet 518heeft", Judges 11:25), a zero for a letter in the Finnish ("kuka 0n", Proverbs 30:4), "×" for "ł" in the Polish, stray signs in the Persian and the Japanese ("／" in 24 verses, and "モ−セ" for "モーセ", so a search for Moses missed 2 verses), a Latin "w" for a Hebrew letter in 2 verses, ",." and ".," in 18 Swahili, Tamil and Polish verses, and 169 missing spaces after a full stop or semicolon (141 in the Synodal: "Симовых;Ханаан"). Clean-up no longer leaves a space before a full stop where it removes the Arabic Bible's invisible marks or gap stars (4 verses), or glues two sentences where it removes another numbering's verse number (2 psalm titles in the Synodal).
- **Book names**: the Swahili Bible showed 1 John as "1Yohana 1 3:16", and three more numbered books had no space; the Danish showed Ruth and Job in capitals and misspelled Colossians; the Dutch had "Numberi" and "2 Corinthiër". They now read as printed, and Find also takes "1 Kongebog", "Salmerne", "Richteren", "Sędziów" and "Yakobo".
- **Bold in search results** now covers the marks on a word's last letter (an Arabic shadda was left out of the bold).
- **A favorites or history file nested too deeply** (100,000 brackets) stopped the app at startup. It is now kept aside as damaged, like any other file that can't be read.
- **OK and Cancel in Customize Colors** were in English whatever the menu language. They now follow it.
- **A new menu language** now reaches the windows that are open (About, Customize Colors and prayers, which keep the colors you picked but did not apply yet). Before, they stayed in the old language. A message that no Bible could be loaded is shown in the menu language too.
- **Prayers**: choosing a prayer that is already open brings its window forward instead of opening a second one on top of it, and prayer windows open on the widget's screen instead of the main one.
- **A Bible file you add** with a superscript digit as a verse number now loses only that verse instead of being skipped whole, and a verse that holds only another numbering's verse number, such as "(H40:19)", is left out instead of showing as an empty passage.
- **Arabic text on the widget** was drawn with letter spacing, which pulls joined letters apart and broke ligatures such as الله. Arabic, Hebrew and Persian verses and references now have none, on the widget, in the prayer window and in saved images.
- **The verse timer could stop for good**: if showing one verse failed, no new verse came until a restart. The timer now always carries on.
- **Daily mode and changing translation**: switching translations in Daily mode showed a random verse instead of the verse of the day. It now keeps the verse of the day.
- **Damaged Bible files**: a Bible file with bad data no longer stops the widget; it is skipped and noted in `widget.log`.
- **Prayer window keys**: the arrow keys and Esc now work even after clicking into the prayer text.
- **Dragging the widget**: each snap no longer leaves a used animation behind (100 drags left 100; now 1).
- **Two copies at once**: starting the widget twice at the same moment could leave both running. A lock file now keeps it to one.
- **Waking from sleep**: if the PC slept past midnight (Daily mode) or past the next change, the new verse could come late. The widget now compares the clock every 30 seconds and changes the verse straight away.
- **stop_widget.bat**: after a crash it could stop an unrelated program that had been given the widget's old process number, even another Python program. It now checks by the process's command line that it is the widget, and a `widget.pid` holding anything but a number is ignored.
- **Running from source with two versions of Python**: `dependencies.bat` could install PySide6 into one while `start_widget.vbs` started the widget with the other, which then failed without a message. Both now use the same one (the newest Python 3 the py launcher knows, or else the one on the PATH).
- **Files saved with a byte order mark** (by PowerShell or some versions of Notepad): `bibles/index.json` lost every translation's display name, and `translation.txt`, `language.txt`, `mode.txt` and `corner.txt` were ignored, so those settings went back to their defaults. They are now read either way.
- **Customize Colors sometimes did nothing**: if the colors window had been minimized (Win+D minimizes it), choosing Customize Colors again left it minimized and invisible. It now comes back every time: 3 of 3 test runs, up from 0 of 3.
- **A hand-edited `bibles/index.json` saved in ANSI** (as older editors do, for example with "Português" in it) stopped the app at startup, as did one of the wrong shape. It is now read either way, and an entry it can't use is skipped. The same goes for `book_names.json`, `prayers.json` and `colors.txt`, which also keeps a comment written in ANSI intact when a color is saved. On Japanese, Chinese or Korean Windows, a byte that the system's code page can't read in `colors.txt` or `updates.txt` no longer stops the app starting.
- **Settings could be lost**: if the app was ended while saving (on a crash or power cut), the translation, menu language, mode, colors or position could be left empty and go back to their defaults. Each is now replaced in one step, so the file holds either the old setting or the new one. Saving a color also keeps comments and anything else you wrote in `colors.txt`.

---

### Download
Download `BibleWidget-2.1.0-win64.zip`, unzip it anywhere you can write to, and run `BibleWidget.exe`. No install and no Python needed. Its SHA-256 checksum is in `BibleWidget-2.1.0-win64.zip.sha256`.

releases.name: Faraday 3.0.0
releases.body:
Faraday 3.0.0 is a brand new desktop app on a hardened vault core. Free, fully offline, open source.

![Faraday overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/puretechteam/project-faraday/v3.0.0/docs/screenshots/overview.png)

## Highlights

- **New desktop app (PySide6):** one list and detail view for every entry type, command palette (Ctrl+K), password and passphrase generator, overview with health checks, backups, access log and threat model.
- **Live two-factor codes** for stored authenticator secrets, with a countdown.
- **Import** from Bitwarden, KeePass, KeePassXC or another Faraday vault, and **encrypted export** to a single password-protected `.faraday` file. There is no plain-text export.
- **14 themes**, including every classic theme from earlier versions, picked from a preview gallery.
- **Safer by default:** auto-lock clears the screen and the clipboard, locks when Windows locks, and copied secrets stay out of Windows clipboard history.

## Vault safety

- Crash-safe atomic saves, plus an automatic encrypted snapshot before every change.
- A lock file stops two windows (or a window and the CLI) from writing the same vault.
- A vault changed on disk by another program is never silently overwritten.
- Fields and entry types from newer versions are preserved.
- The file format is unchanged (version 1): vaults from 2.x open as they are.

## Install

**Windows app:** download `Faraday-3.0.0-windows-x64.zip`, unzip it anywhere and run `Faraday.exe`. No Python needed.

**From source:** `pip install -e .` then `faraday gui` (Python 3.10+).

New vaults are created in `Documents\Faraday` by default. Back up your vault before upgrading, and keep your master password safe: it cannot be recovered.

Full details in the [changelog](https://github.com/puretechteam/project-faraday/blob/v3.0.0/CHANGELOG.md).

releases.body:
# Changelog - Faraday 2.0.0

## Version 2.0.0 - April 23, 2026
- UI and theming overhaul
  - Replaced the native Windows menubar with an in-window themed strip (File, Security, Theme, Help) so it follows the selected theme.
  - Added theme settings, quick presets, and persistent local theme save/load via `%LOCALAPPDATA%\FaradayVault\gui_theme.json`.
  - **User impact:** consistent theming across navigation and dialogs, including on Windows.

- Security actions and access guard improvements
  - Added optional Action PIN workflow from the Security menu (set up / change / disable).
  - Added guard checks for sensitive actions (copy, reveal, delete, export-style flows) across sections.
  - Improved protected dialogs for long secret content with better scrolling/readability.
  - **User impact:** sensitive actions can require an extra unlock step without changing master-password flow.

- Vault operations, safety, and reliability updates
  - Added `Backup Vault` flow from the File menu.
  - Updated open-vault prompt to remove generator access in that path (`show_generate_password=False`).
  - Fixed auto-lock worker crash (`RuntimeError: cannot join current thread`) by preventing self-join in the lock path.
  - Added offline structure audit script (`scripts/audit_vault_structure.py`) for envelope/header sanity checks.
  - **User impact:** safer backup/lock flow, cleaner open-vault UX, and improved auto-lock stability.

- Data model and section capability expansion
  - Identity: added optional SSN support, made email validation conditional when email is present, and guarded SSN copy behavior.
  - Documents: added category support in model/UI (including ID/Driver License-style categories).
  - Two-factor: improved scrollable presentation and safer reveal/copy UX for codes.
  - Completed guard wiring across credentials, secure notes, and Wi-Fi sensitive actions.
  - **User impact:** broader real-world record support with stronger consistency on protected actions.

- Threat model and educational analysis panel
  - Added a dedicated `Threat model` tab with honest scope/disclaimers, vault KDF metadata, local Argon2 timing benchmarks, and clearer quantum wording.
  - Added metadata-only credential/Wi-Fi analysis cards (length + naive entropy context; no plaintext password display).
  - Updated scenario table with clearer labels, 200/300-bit rows, improved resizing/scrolling, unified duration wording, and hundredths precision.
  - **User impact:** clearer security context and strength guidance without exposing stored secrets.
